baselineEntries.text: DA + ActionSA: Joburg’s exes are trying again. Hide the old screenshots.
baselineEntries.when: DA + ActionSA selected · Johannesburg
baselineEntries.basis: DA and ActionSA were Joburg partners who publicly fell out over coalition talks. Exes and screenshots are fictional breakup imagery.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: DA and ActionSA were partners in Johannesburg’s governing coalition. In January 2023, ActionSA publicly criticised the DA’s coalition negotiations and proposed putting forward its own mayoral candidate.

baselineEntries.text: DA + ActionSA in Tshwane: same exes, same keys, fresh trust issues.
baselineEntries.when: DA + ActionSA selected · Tshwane
baselineEntries.basis: ActionSA withdrew support from Tshwane’s DA-led coalition in September 2024. The joke treats a new deal as getting back with an ex.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: ActionSA announced its withdrawal of support from Tshwane’s DA-led coalition in September 2024. Its own statement cited the city’s finances; that was the party’s stated explanation.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + ActionSA: Tshwane’s anti-ANC speeches have been placed on unpaid leave.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + ActionSA selected · Tshwane
baselineEntries.basis: ActionSA had joined an anti-ANC national pact, but ANC support helped Moya become Tshwane mayor. Unpaid leave means setting those earlier speeches aside.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: ActionSA joined the August 2023 Multi-Party Charter aimed at replacing the ANC government. The ANC then backed ActionSA’s Nasiphi Moya for Tshwane mayor in October 2024. She was elected on 9 October, illustrating how local partners can differ from earlier national alignments.

baselineEntries.text: DA + PA in Joburg: the handshake comes with a counteroffer.
baselineEntries.when: DA + PA selected · Johannesburg
baselineEntries.basis: Talks to restore PA support for Joburg’s DA-led coalition broke down in January 2023. The joke is about hard bargaining, not an actual extra offer shown on screen.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: Talks to restore PA support for Johannesburg’s DA-led coalition broke down in January 2023. DA mayor Mpho Phalatse subsequently lost a no-confidence vote. Accounts of responsibility were disputed.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + EFF in Joburg: enemies on the posters, colleagues at the photocopier.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + EFF selected · Johannesburg
baselineEntries.basis: ANC and EFF joined Joburg’s wider unity coalition in 2023 despite competing against each other. Photocopier colleagues means sharing an administration.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: Johannesburg’s 2022/23 annual reporting lists both the ANC and EFF in the Government of Local Unity formed in January 2023, alongside several smaller parties.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + IFP: KZN’s old rivals now arguing over who booked the meeting room.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + IFP selected · KwaZulu-Natal
baselineEntries.basis: The old rivals cooperated in the 2024 KZN government. The meeting-room argument is invented everyday rivalry.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.note: The current source URL is an IFP June 28 statement whose previously extracted text mainly covers national GNU talks. Recheck that it actually supports the provincial wording, or add a direct KZN source.
baselineEntries.fact: In June 2024, the IFP announced cooperation with the ANC and DA nationally and a provincial arrangement with the ANC, DA and NFP in KwaZulu-Natal. This was a provincial deal, not a blanket municipal agreement.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + DA: the attack ads must make excellent Cabinet icebreakers.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + DA selected · Any municipality (national backstory)
baselineEntries.basis: ANC and DA entered the 2024 GNU after years as opponents. Old campaign attacks would make awkward conversation between new colleagues.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: The ANC and DA joined the national Government of National Unity in June 2024. National cooperation does not establish an agreement in this municipality.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + MK: family reunion. Bring your own faction.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + MK selected · Any municipality (national backstory)
baselineEntries.basis: Zuma’s move from former ANC president to backing MK split a political family. Bring your own faction mocks that shared history and rivalry.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: Former ANC president Jacob Zuma backed MK in December 2023. The ANC announced his suspension in January 2024 over support for another party. That history informs the reunion joke, not a prediction of this deal.

baselineEntries.text: DA + FF+: the anti-ANC carpool now stops at Cabinet.
baselineEntries.when: DA + FF+ selected · Any municipality (national backstory)
baselineEntries.basis: DA and FF+ joined the anti-ANC Charter, then the ANC-inclusive GNU. The carpool changed destination.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: DA and FF+ participated in the August 2023 Multi-Party Charter talks aimed at replacing the ANC government. Both were then named as participants in the ANC-inclusive national GNU in June 2024. These national precedents do not confirm a local coalition.

baselineEntries.text: DA + PA: one GNU, two parties refusing to let the other finish a sentence.
baselineEntries.when: DA + PA selected · Any municipality (national backstory)
baselineEntries.basis: DA and PA both joined the GNU. Interrupting each other is a fictional personality joke, not a sourced incident.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: The DA and PA were both named in the national GNU in June 2024. Parties can cooperate nationally while competing or bargaining differently in individual councils.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + EFF in Ekurhuleni: less couples’ counselling, more crowd control.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + EFF selected · Ekurhuleni
baselineEntries.basis: ANC and EFF’s Ekurhuleni arrangement faced a disrupted council sitting and threatened breakup in 2024. The relationship metaphor exaggerates that friction.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: ANC and EFF governed together in Ekurhuleni in 2023–2024. In March 2024, ANC representatives publicly threatened to end the arrangement after a disrupted council sitting. Their explanations were political claims, not an agreed account of blame.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + EFF in the Bay: they brought the votes. Someone else got the big chair.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + EFF selected · Nelson Mandela Bay
baselineEntries.basis: ANC and EFF helped replace Nelson Mandela Bay’s DA mayor with Northern Alliance’s Gary van Niekerk in 2023. Their votes put a third party in the top job.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: In May 2023, a coalition including ANC and EFF helped replace DA mayor Retief Odendaal with Gary van Niekerk of the Northern Alliance. Van Niekerk had been council speaker. This is a historical leadership change, not today’s coalition map.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + PA in Knysna: handle this reunion like an oyster. Carefully, and on ice.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + PA selected · Knysna
baselineEntries.basis: PA withdrew from Knysna’s ANC-led coalition in 2023. The oyster reference is a local Knysna image for a delicate reunion.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.note: Knysna oysters are recognisable locally, but “carefully, and on ice” may be a thin political punchline.
baselineEntries.fact: In September 2023, PA councillors resigned from Knysna’s mayoral committee and the party announced its withdrawal from the ANC-led coalition. The PA linked its decision to senior appointments; that was its stated reason.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + EFF in Durban: revolutionary until the mayor needs a favour.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + EFF selected · eThekwini
baselineEntries.basis: EFF votes helped defeat a no-confidence motion against ANC mayor Kaunda in 2023. It contrasts revolutionary rhetoric with supporting an ANC officeholder.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: EFF councillors voted against a no-confidence motion targeting ANC mayor Mxolisi Kaunda in February 2023. The motion failed. Supporting a mayor in that vote did not by itself establish a formal coalition agreement.

baselineEntries.text: DA + ActionSA: signed the pact. Kept the grudge.
baselineEntries.when: DA + ActionSA selected · Any municipality (national backstory)
baselineEntries.basis: DA and ActionSA signed the 2023 Charter despite a difficult relationship. The grudge is comic interpretation, not a clause in the pact.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: DA and ActionSA were among the signatories to the Multi-Party Charter in August 2023, ahead of the 2024 national and provincial elections. This was a national pact, not evidence of a deal in this council.

baselineEntries.text: DA + IFP: the anti-ANC pact took a scenic route through the GNU.
baselineEntries.when: DA + IFP selected · Any municipality (national backstory)
baselineEntries.basis: DA and IFP signed the anti-ANC Charter and later joined the GNU. Scenic route means ending up sharing government with the ANC.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: DA and IFP signed the August 2023 Multi-Party Charter and both joined the national GNU in June 2024. Those national arrangements do not establish a municipal coalition.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + PA: the GNU is a team sport. Both have appointed themselves captain.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + PA selected · Any municipality (national backstory)
baselineEntries.basis: ANC and PA joined the GNU. Both calling themselves captain is an invented joke about competing egos.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: ANC and PA were named as participants in the national GNU in June 2024. This national history does not confirm a coalition in this municipality.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + ActionSA in Joburg: commitment issues, but make them a council policy.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + ActionSA selected · Johannesburg
baselineEntries.basis: ANC and ActionSA agreed to issue-by-issue cooperation in Joburg in 2024. Commitment issues means stopping short of an unrestricted coalition commitment.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: ANC and ActionSA agreed to cooperate issue by issue in Johannesburg in August 2024. ActionSA’s Nobuhle Mthembu was elected speaker on 21 August. Issue-by-issue support was distinct from an unrestricted coalition commitment.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + Al Jama-ah: the junior partner took the master bedroom.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + Al Jama-ah selected · Johannesburg
baselineEntries.basis: Al Jama-ah supplied Joburg’s mayor in the broader ANC-backed unity coalition. The junior partner getting the main bedroom means a small party taking the top office.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: Al Jama-ah’s Thapelo Amad became Johannesburg mayor in January 2023 under the Government of Local Unity, which included the ANC and EFF. The city’s annual report records his resignation in April 2023.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + COPE in Tshwane: barely a caucus. Somehow the head of the table.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + COPE selected · Tshwane
baselineEntries.basis: ANC and EFF helped elect COPE’s Makwarela as Tshwane mayor in February 2023. A very small party obtained the senior role.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: Tshwane elected COPE’s Murunwa Makwarela mayor on 28 February 2023. ATM nominated him, with ANC and EFF support. This records that election, not an enduring agreement between all those parties.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + EFF: booked the Tshwane honeymoon. COPE got the suite.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + EFF selected · Tshwane
baselineEntries.basis: ANC and EFF supported a COPE mayor in Tshwane in 2023. They supplied support while another party got the mayoralty.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: ANC and EFF supported COPE’s Murunwa Makwarela in Tshwane’s February 2023 mayoral election. He defeated the DA’s Cilliers Brink by 112 votes to 101. Voting together did not itself establish a permanent coalition.

baselineEntries.text: DA + EFF in Ekurhuleni: the ex brought the mayoral chair back. Don’t ask.
baselineEntries.when: DA + EFF selected · Ekurhuleni
baselineEntries.basis: EFF votes helped return DA mayor Tania Campbell to office in November 2022. It was voting support, not proof of a formal DA–EFF coalition.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: After ANC–EFF talks failed, EFF votes helped return DA mayor Tania Campbell to office on 8 November 2022, two weeks after her removal. This was voting support for a minority administration, not proof of a formal DA–EFF coalition.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + ABC: Durban’s deputy job came with an ejector seat.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + ABC selected · eThekwini
baselineEntries.basis: ANC brought the motion that removed ABC’s Philani Mavundla as eThekwini deputy mayor in 2022. Ejector seat means a precarious coalition post.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: ABC leader Philani Mavundla lost his eThekwini executive-committee position and deputy mayoralty in December 2022. The ANC brought the removal motion; the council minutes record ANC and EFF votes in favour.

baselineEntries.text: DA + IFP in Durban: so united, one stayed off the ballot.
baselineEntries.when: DA + IFP selected · eThekwini
baselineEntries.basis: DA and IFP agreed not to compete with each other in a particular eThekwini by-election. Cooperation meant one party standing aside in that ward.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: Ahead of eThekwini’s December 2022 ward 99 by-election, the DA and IFP arranged not to compete against each other there. The IFP won the ward from the ANC. A ward-level electoral arrangement is not a citywide governing coalition.

baselineEntries.text: DA + ACDP: Cape Town’s coalition needed seven parties and possibly a prayer.
baselineEntries.when: DA + ACDP selected · Cape Town
baselineEntries.basis: ACDP joined Cape Town’s seven-party coalition in 2006. The prayer is a wordplay on the party’s Christian identity, not a claim about a religious event.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: In 2006, the DA assembled a seven-party Cape Town coalition including the ACDP, FF+ and UDM. Helen Zille became mayor and ACDP councillor Andrew Arnolds became deputy mayor.

baselineEntries.text: DA + FF+ in Cape Town: seven parties, one bell. FF+ called dibs.
baselineEntries.when: DA + FF+ selected · Cape Town
baselineEntries.basis: FF+ joined that seven-party Cape Town coalition and supplied the Speaker. The bell stands for control of debate.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: The FF+ joined Cape Town’s DA-led seven-party coalition in 2006. Its councillor Dirk Smit became speaker. This historical coalition predates the DA’s later outright city majorities.

baselineEntries.text: Cape Town’s DA: six ex-partners omitted from the solo-career documentary.
baselineEntries.when: DA selected · Cape Town
baselineEntries.basis: The DA needed six partners to govern Cape Town in 2006. The solo-career joke teases later narratives of governing alone.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.note: “Omitted from the documentary” is fictional; there is no evidence of an actual documentary omitting partners.
baselineEntries.fact: The DA needed six partner parties to form Cape Town’s governing coalition in 2006. Helen Zille won the mayoral vote 106–103. This is an earlier chapter, not a description of the present council.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + DA in Mangaung: the ANC caucus took “opposition” a bit too literally.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + DA selected · Mangaung
baselineEntries.basis: Some ANC councillors backed DA’s Maryke Davies for Mangaung Speaker against their party’s choice in 2023. Opposition here came from within the ANC.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: DA councillor Maryke Davies became Mangaung speaker in March 2023. News24 reported that ANC councillors voted against their party’s choice. These were cross-party votes, not an ANC–DA coalition agreement.

baselineEntries.text: Mangaung ANC: enough seats to govern. Not enough to agree with itself.
baselineEntries.when: ANC selected · Mangaung
baselineEntries.basis: ANC councillors split over Mangaung’s Speaker vote. A numerical majority did not guarantee internal agreement.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: In March 2023, some ANC councillors backed the DA’s Maryke Davies for Mangaung speaker against their party’s choice, according to contemporary reporting. The episode illustrates internal caucus discipline, not a formal coalition.

baselineEntries.text: Buffalo City ANC: no opposition required. The recall is coming from inside the house.
baselineEntries.when: ANC selected · Buffalo City
baselineEntries.basis: ANC recalled its own Buffalo City mayor in 2023. The opposition did not need to trigger that leadership change.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: The ANC recalled Buffalo City mayor Xola Pakati in March 2023. Princess Faku replaced him on 23 March, winning 62 votes to the DA candidate’s 22. The ANC held a majority; this was an internal leadership change, not a coalition collapse.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + ATM in Mogale: the junior partner ordered the executive package.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + ATM selected · Mogale City
baselineEntries.basis: ATM’s Danny Thupane became mayor under an ATM–ANC–EFF arrangement in Mogale City in 2023. Executive package means the top office.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: Mogale City elected ATM’s Danny Thupane mayor in April 2023, replacing the DA-led administration. The municipality named ATM, ANC and EFF as participants in the new Government of Local Unity.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + EFF in Mogale: big parties negotiating who gets to call the ATM mayor “boss”.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + EFF selected · Mogale City
baselineEntries.basis: ANC and EFF joined an arrangement that gave Mogale’s mayoralty to ATM. Boss is comic shorthand for the mayor, not a legal chain of command between parties.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: Mogale City’s April 2023 leadership change installed an ATM mayor, ANC speaker and EFF council whip. The official statement described an ATM–ANC–EFF Government of Local Unity.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + PA in Emfuleni: the ANC’s majority now comes with terms and conditions.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + PA selected · Emfuleni
baselineEntries.basis: After ANC lost its outright majority, PA and local parties helped it govern Emfuleni. Terms and conditions means having to bargain with partners.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: MISTRA’s record of Emfuleni’s November 2021 administration lists ANC, PA and several community parties as governing partners. The ANC had lost its outright council majority. This refers to the arrangement at its formation.

sources.label: MISTRA dataset · Emfuleni EMF_01, formed 22 Nov 2021

baselineEntries.text: ANC + AIC in Rustenburg: tiny caucus. Platinum-sized demands.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + AIC selected · Rustenburg
baselineEntries.basis: AIC and Arona helped ANC reach a majority in Rustenburg after 2021. Platinum references the area; no actual monetary demand is alleged.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.note: “Platinum-sized demands” is invented exaggeration. The source establishes bargaining importance, not a particular demand or payment.
baselineEntries.fact: After the 2021 election, Rustenburg’s ANC formed a governing arrangement with the AIC and local party Arona. MISTRA records how small-party support helped the ANC reach a council majority.

sources.label: MISTRA Coalitions Barometer · 2021–2023, North West chapter

baselineEntries.text: ANC + PA in JB Marks: almost a majority is a very expensive almost.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + PA selected · JB Marks
baselineEntries.basis: ANC was one seat short of a majority in JB Marks; PA’s two seats supplied the support. Expensive means political bargaining power, not a proven payment.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: In the 2021 JB Marks election, the ANC won 33 of 67 seats, one below an outright majority. Its coalition with the PA, which held two seats, crossed that threshold.

sources.label: MISTRA Coalitions Barometer · 2021–2023, North West chapter

baselineEntries.text: ANC + PA in Ditsobotla: that mayoral term barely outlasted a Home Affairs queue.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + PA selected · Ditsobotla
baselineEntries.basis: A new PA mayor announced her resignation within hours in 2023. The Home Affairs queue is an exaggerated familiar comparison, not measured timing.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: PA’s newly elected Ditsobotla mayor announced her resignation within hours in January 2023, amid a dispute over a municipal-manager appointment. This followed an ANC–PA-led agreement after the December 2022 rerun election.

baselineEntries.text: LCF + EFF in Standerton: the residents’ meeting has developed mayoral ambitions.
baselineEntries.when: LCF + EFF selected · Lekwa
baselineEntries.basis: Lekwa Community Forum won mayor and Speaker with EFF taking chief whip in 2021. The local movement’s meeting became a governing team.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: After the 2021 election, Lekwa Community Forum candidates won the mayor and speaker positions, while an EFF councillor became chief whip. The result ended ANC control of the municipality.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + EFF in Sasolburg: local chemistry. Head office said absolutely not.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + EFF selected · Metsimaholo
baselineEntries.basis: An EFF mayor elected with ANC support resigned after EFF national leadership objected. Local chemistry is also a nod to Sasolburg’s industrial identity.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: EFF mayor Selloane Motjeane resigned in November 2021 after her party’s national leadership objected to her election with ANC support. The DA’s Jeff Zwane succeeded her in December. Local support and national instructions had diverged.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + AIC in Sasolburg: little party, big chain. Must be quite heavy.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + AIC selected · Metsimaholo
baselineEntries.basis: AIC’s Jack Malindi became mayor with ANC and ATM support in 2023. The chain stands for a large role obtained by a small party.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: AIC councillor Jack Malindi became Metsimaholo mayor in August 2023 after DA mayor Jeff Zwane’s removal. SABC reported ANC and ATM support for Malindi’s election.

baselineEntries.text: MAP16 + EFF: nothing says trust like giving your partner the audit job.
baselineEntries.when: MAP16 + EFF selected · Maluti a Phofung
baselineEntries.basis: EFF agreed to oversee public accounts while supporting MAP16’s leadership rather than formally co-governing. The audit joke is about oversight within a support arrangement.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.note: Public-accounts oversight is not literally an audit appointment. “Audit job” may oversimplify the role.
baselineEntries.fact: MAP16 secured a November 2021 agreement to lead Maluti-a-Phofung with backing from the EFF and smaller parties. MAP16 said the EFF would oversee public accounts rather than co-govern. The DA and FF+ offered support for electing officeholders without joining the agreement.

baselineEntries.text: IFP + Team Sugar: a ballot withdrawal with extra sweetness.
baselineEntries.when: IFP + TSSA selected · Newcastle
baselineEntries.basis: IFP stood aside for Team Sugar in one Newcastle by-election in 2023. Sweetness is a pun on Team Sugar’s name.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.note: The sweet-name pun is easy to understand but fairly mild; the actual ward arrangement is more interesting than the punchline.
baselineEntries.fact: In February 2023, the IFP agreed not to contest Newcastle’s ward 31 by-election and to support coalition partner Team Sugar South Africa. The partners publicly confirmed the arrangement and denied that it had been forced by threats.

baselineEntries.text: Newcastle’s IFP: please support us. By voting for someone else.
baselineEntries.when: IFP selected · Newcastle
baselineEntries.basis: IFP supported Team Sugar rather than fielding a candidate in one ward. The contradictory voting instruction is the joke.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.note: Only one by-election ward is meant. The joke must not be read as IFP telling all Newcastle voters to choose another party.
baselineEntries.fact: In February 2023 the IFP stood aside in Newcastle’s ward 31 by-election to support Team Sugar South Africa. This is a past electoral arrangement, not evidence that Team Sugar is part of your selected deal.

baselineEntries.text: IFP + EFF in Richards Bay: the mayoral chair wrecked another beautiful friendship.
baselineEntries.when: IFP + EFF selected · uMhlathuze
baselineEntries.basis: The IFP–EFF breakup followed disagreement over EFF’s request to lead uMhlathuze. The coveted chair represents the mayoralty.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.note: The historical request/refusal comes from party accounts. “Beautiful friendship” is sarcasm, not a measured description of trust.
baselineEntries.fact: The IFP and EFF’s local cooperation broke down in January 2023. In its public account of talks, the IFP said it rejected an EFF request to lead uMhlathuze. That is the IFP’s account of the negotiations, not an agreed finding about blame.

baselineEntries.text: DA + IFP in Richards Bay: new deputy, same chair. Mind the previous occupant’s feelings.
baselineEntries.when: DA + IFP selected · uMhlathuze
baselineEntries.basis: A DA deputy mayor served under an IFP mayor after the earlier EFF deputy departed in 2023. The old occupant is the previous EFF role-holder.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: DA councillor Christo Botha became uMhlathuze deputy mayor in August 2023 under IFP mayor Xolani Ngwezi. ACCORD’s timeline records support from IFP, DA and smaller parties, after the earlier EFF deputy’s departure.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + ABC in Greytown: Mavundla’s comeback needed a new badge and the old friends.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + ABC selected · uMvoti
baselineEntries.basis: Philani Mavundla returned as uMvoti mayor under ABC with ANC support, having previously held the post as an ANC member. New badge, old contacts.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: ABC leader Philani Mavundla became uMvoti mayor in June 2023 through an agreement with the ANC. He had previously been the municipality’s mayor as an ANC member. The new arrangement displaced the IFP-led administration.

baselineEntries.text: IFP + ABC in Greytown: the reunion invitation should probably mention the ANC.
baselineEntries.when: IFP + ABC selected · uMvoti
baselineEntries.basis: ABC moved from an IFP–ABC–DA arrangement to an ANC-backed arrangement in 2023. The ANC is the awkward recent partner at the reunion.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: An IFP–ABC–DA arrangement governed uMvoti after the 2021 election. In June 2023, ABC switched to an agreement with the ANC and its leader Philani Mavundla became mayor.

baselineEntries.text: DA + EFF in Modimolle: heads, principles. Tails, a mayor.
baselineEntries.when: DA + EFF selected · Modimolle-Mookgophong
baselineEntries.basis: A tied 2021 mayoral election was settled by a coin toss after EFF and FF+ supported the DA candidate. Heads and tails are literal historical references.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: Marlene van Staden was re-elected Modimolle-Mookgophong mayor in December 2021 after tied votes were settled by a coin toss. EFF and FF+ councillors had supported the DA candidate. This records voting support, not a formal DA–EFF coalition.

baselineEntries.text: DA + FF+ in Modimolle: when the kingmaker is loose change.
baselineEntries.when: DA + FF+ selected · Modimolle-Mookgophong
baselineEntries.basis: The same mayoral tie was settled by a coin. Loose change was the tiebreaker; no particular denomination is claimed.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: The DA reported that EFF and FF+ councillors backed Marlene van Staden in December 2021. Two mayoral votes tied at 14–14 before a coin toss settled the election. The game keeps its usual majority threshold.

baselineEntries.text: DA + EFF in Thabazimbi: the coalition drama outlived the council.
baselineEntries.when: DA + EFF selected · Thabazimbi
baselineEntries.basis: EFF left the original DA-led arrangement; prolonged council disputes preceded dissolution in 2024. The drama outliving the council is a compressed timeline joke.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.note: “Outlived the council” compresses a 2021–2024 sequence; it does not establish that DA–EFF cooperation lasted until dissolution.
baselineEntries.fact: MISTRA records EFF participation in Thabazimbi’s initial DA-led 2021 coalition, followed by its departure in 2022. Prolonged disputes over council leadership preceded the council’s dissolution in 2024.

sources.label: MISTRA dataset · Thabazimbi TBZ_01 and TBZ_02

baselineEntries.text: DA + NCM in Springbok: musical chairs with a playlist everyone signed.
baselineEntries.when: DA + NCM selected · NAMA KHOI
baselineEntries.basis: DA and NCM swapped mayor and Speaker positions under an agreed rotation in July 2024. Musical chairs was planned rather than a surprise breakup.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: In July 2024, DA councillor Rodney Kritzinger and NCM councillor Gustav Bock exchanged the mayor and speaker positions. The DA said this implemented the rotation agreed with the Namakwa Civic Movement in 2021.

baselineEntries.text: DA + UDM in the Bay: the deputy mayor’s chair has abandonment issues.
baselineEntries.when: DA + UDM selected · Nelson Mandela Bay
baselineEntries.basis: UDM deputy mayor Mongameli Bobani was removed in 2017 amid a dispute with DA partners. Abandonment issues personifies the deputy’s chair.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: DA and UDM were partners in Nelson Mandela Bay’s post-2016 coalition, alongside ACDP and COPE. In August 2017, a no-confidence vote removed UDM deputy mayor Mongameli Bobani, deepening the dispute between the partners.

baselineEntries.text: DA + FF+ in George: broke up, got back together, definitely kept the screenshots.
baselineEntries.when: DA + FF+ selected · George
baselineEntries.basis: DA ended its FF+ coalition in 2024 and announced a new agreement in 2025. Screenshots are imagined breakup baggage.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: The DA ended its George coalition with the FF+ in June 2024. In November 2025 it announced a new agreement with FF+ and ACDP, including an FF+ deputy mayor. These are dated changes, not a claim about the current administration.

baselineEntries.text: DA + ACDP in George: prayers answered. The answer was Corporate Services.
baselineEntries.when: DA + ACDP selected · George
baselineEntries.basis: ACDP received George’s Corporate Services portfolio under a 2025 agreement. Prayer is a pun on the Christian party’s identity; the portfolio is the real hook.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.note: A religious pun rather than a scandal or ideological claim. Some readers may find it too gentle or repetitive.
baselineEntries.fact: The DA’s November 2025 George coalition announcement named ACDP and FF+ as partners. It allocated the corporate-services mayoral-committee portfolio to ACDP. This is the announced agreement at that date.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + FF+ in Oudtshoorn: awkward enough to make an ostrich look away.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + FF+ selected · Oudtshoorn
baselineEntries.basis: FF+ took Oudtshoorn’s mayoralty with ANC and other parties in 2024. The ostrich is local imagery for the surprising partnership.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: FF+ councillor Johan Allers became Oudtshoorn mayor in August 2024 under a new arrangement including ANC, PA and local parties, after the DA mayor’s removal. ANC councillor Mziwoxolo Tyatya became deputy mayor.

baselineEntries.text: DA + FF+ in Oudtshoorn: even the ostriches saw that breakup coming.
baselineEntries.when: DA + FF+ selected · Oudtshoorn
baselineEntries.basis: FF+ backed removal of a DA mayor and joined an ANC-backed arrangement. The ostrich joke refers to the area and the political breakup.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.note: “Saw it coming” is invented hindsight, not evidence that the breakup was publicly predictable.
baselineEntries.fact: In July 2024 the FF+ backed a no-confidence motion against DA mayor Chris Macpherson. Its Johan Allers became mayor in August with ANC and other parties, ending the earlier DA–FF+ partnership in Oudtshoorn.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + GOOD in Theewaterskloof: GOOD company. Until it found other company.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + GOOD selected · Theewaterskloof
baselineEntries.basis: GOOD left its ANC–PA alignment and backed a DA-led arrangement in 2024. Company is a pun on both companionship and the party name.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: GOOD helped the ANC and PA govern Theewaterskloof after the 2021 election. In August 2024, GOOD changed alignment and backed the DA, resulting in new mayoral and speaker appointments.

baselineEntries.text: DA + GOOD in Theewaterskloof: the ANC’s ex says you’re different.
baselineEntries.when: DA + GOOD selected · Theewaterskloof
baselineEntries.basis: GOOD switched from ANC/PA to DA support in 2024. The former partner’s reassurance is an invented relationship joke.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: GOOD backed a DA-led arrangement in Theewaterskloof in August 2024 after leaving its alignment with ANC and PA. GOOD’s John Michels became speaker and the DA’s Lincoln de Bruyn became mayor.

baselineEntries.text: DA + PDC in Plett: your coalition partner checked into the other mayoral suite.
baselineEntries.when: DA + PDC selected · Bitou
baselineEntries.basis: PDC left a DA-led arrangement; its councillor became mayor in an ANC-aligned arrangement in 2024. The hotel suite is a Plett-flavoured office metaphor.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: The DA, Plett Democratic Congress and Active United Front formed Bitou’s post-2021 coalition. PDC left in early 2024, and its Claude Terblanche became mayor under an ANC-aligned arrangement in February.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + PA in Plett: the coalition has a stricter checkout time than your holiday flat.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + PA selected · Bitou
baselineEntries.basis: ANC, PA and others formed a Bitou arrangement in February 2024 that changed again later that year. Checkout compares coalition turnover with a holiday stay.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: In February 2024, ANC, PA, PDC and IPM formed the arrangement that replaced Bitou’s DA-led administration. PDC councillor Claude Terblanche became mayor. The arrangement changed again later that year.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + PA in Beaufort West: the mayoral chain gets more mileage than the N1.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + PA selected · Beaufort West
baselineEntries.basis: Beaufort West saw repeated mayoral changes under the post-2021 arrangement. The N1 is a local travel reference; mileage is obvious exaggeration.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: Beaufort West’s post-2021 coalition included ANC, PA and Karoo Democratic Force. Several mayoral changes followed; by February 2024, reporting described another change as the municipality’s fifth mayor in under three years.

baselineEntries.text: DA + Cederberg First: got back together. The mountains have heard this one before.
baselineEntries.when: DA + CFRA selected · Cederberg
baselineEntries.basis: Cederberg First’s mayor returned with earlier DA/FF+ partners in 2023 after a change of administration. The mountains are local scenery, not part of the political claim.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: Cederberg First, DA and FF+ formed a coalition after the 2021 election. After a change of administration in 2022, Cederberg First’s Ruben Richards returned as mayor in March 2023 with the earlier partners.

baselineEntries.text: DA + FF+ in Swellendam: one councillor left. The whole seating plan needed therapy.
baselineEntries.when: DA + FF+ selected · Swellendam
baselineEntries.basis: FF+’s lone councillor abstained and resigned amid a tied mayoral vote in 2025. One person disrupted the entire plan.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.note: The councillor abstained and then resigned. It was not necessarily the entire FF+ party deciding on a walkout.
baselineEntries.fact: In February 2025, Swellendam’s mayoral vote tied 5–5 when FF+ speaker Juan van Schalkwyk abstained and then resigned. The DA and ANC each held five seats; FF+ held one. Party leaders had sought agreement, but the councillor did not follow it.

baselineEntries.text: DA + FF+ in Saldanha: one seat. Suddenly everyone remembers your birthday.
baselineEntries.when: DA + FF+ selected · Saldanha Bay
baselineEntries.basis: DA had 13 of 27 seats after 2021; FF+’s one seat delivered a majority. Remembering a birthday means suddenly courting a pivotal small partner.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: After the 2021 election, Saldanha Bay’s DA held 13 of 27 council seats. Its coalition with FF+, which held one seat, reached the 14-seat majority. These are historical seat figures, separate from your selected deal.

baselineEntries.text: Witzenberg’s DA: kept the receipt for the mayoral chair.
baselineEntries.when: DA selected · Witzenberg
baselineEntries.basis: DA returned to the mayoralty in December 2023. Keeping the receipt jokes about reclaiming an office; the source does not identify an exact partner lineup.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: Trevor Abrahams was elected Witzenberg executive mayor on 14 December 2023. Contemporary reporting described the DA’s return after an ANC-aligned administration. The municipality confirms the appointment date; this story does not infer the exact partner lineup.

baselineEntries.text: DA + FF+ in Langeberg: irreconcilable differences, itemised.
baselineEntries.when: DA + FF+ selected · Langeberg
baselineEntries.basis: DA said FF+’s refusal to support the budget contributed to their 2024 breakup. Itemised turns a budget dispute into a breakup joke.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.note: The stated reason for the breakup is attributed to the DA, not an agreed account of fault.
baselineEntries.fact: The DA and FF+ formed Langeberg’s post-2021 governing coalition. In August 2024 the DA said the relationship had ended, citing the FF+’s refusal to back the May budget among its reasons. That explanation is attributed to the DA.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + ICOSA: the local honeymoon lasted until the provincial office phoned.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + ICOSA selected · Kannaland
baselineEntries.basis: ANC’s provincial leadership ordered withdrawal from the post-2021 ICOSA arrangement. A local deal was interrupted by higher party leadership.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.note: The joke is about conflict between local and provincial party instructions; do not turn that into a current alliance claim.
baselineEntries.fact: An ANC–ICOSA arrangement followed Kannaland’s November 2021 election. The ANC’s provincial leadership instructed its councillors to withdraw in December. The Dullah Omar Institute documents the resulting changes in council alignments.

baselineEntries.text: DA + CSA in Graaff-Reinet: signed just in time to start arguing about the agenda.
baselineEntries.when: DA + CSA selected · Dr. Beyers Naude
baselineEntries.basis: DA, CSA and FF+ reached their 2021 agreement shortly before the inaugural council meeting. The agenda argument is fictional.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: The DA announced a coalition with Compatriots of South Africa and FF+ shortly before Dr Beyers Naudé’s inaugural November 2021 council meeting. DA’s Ewald Loock became mayor and CSA’s Laughton Hoffman became speaker.

baselineEntries.text: DA + FF+ in Graaff-Reinet: a coalition with the punctuality of a last-minute matric project.
baselineEntries.when: DA + FF+ selected · Dr. Beyers Naude
baselineEntries.basis: The same agreement was reached close to the start of the inaugural meeting. The matric-project comparison teases last-minute completion.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.note: The matric-project metaphor is understandable in SA but not especially party-specific.
baselineEntries.fact: DA, FF+ and Compatriots of South Africa concluded a coalition agreement shortly before Dr Beyers Naudé’s inaugural council meeting on 23 November 2021. The DA’s Ewald Loock was elected mayor.

baselineEntries.text: DA + KIM in Knysna: the coalition had sea views. And an expiry date.
baselineEntries.when: DA + KIM selected · Knysna
baselineEntries.basis: DA and KIM governed after 2021 before being removed in August 2022. The sea-view lease is a local metaphor for a short-lived arrangement.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: DA and Knysna Independent Movement governed together after the 2021 election. Their administration was removed in August 2022, making way for an ANC–PA–EFF arrangement. This is the earlier coalition chapter.

baselineEntries.text: Msunduzi ANC: why wait for the opposition to change your mayor?
baselineEntries.when: ANC selected · Msunduzi
baselineEntries.basis: ANC recalled its own Msunduzi mayor in 2019. The joke is about internal removal rather than opposition pressure.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: The ANC recalled Msunduzi mayor Themba Njilo in August 2019 as part of leadership changes in KwaZulu-Natal municipalities. This is an internal party leadership episode, not a coalition breakup.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + IFP: old rivals, shared Cabinet. The polite smiles must hurt.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + IFP selected · Any municipality (national backstory)
baselineEntries.basis: ANC and IFP joined the 2024 GNU despite their history as rivals. Painful polite smiles are invented imagery.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: ANC and IFP were named as participants in the national GNU in June 2024. The appointments included IFP’s Velenkosini Hlabisa at Cooperative Governance, PA’s Gayton McKenzie at Sport, Arts and Culture, and FF+’s Pieter Groenewald at Correctional Services. This does not establish a local coalition.

baselineEntries.text: ANC + FF+: even the old campaign posters have requested a transfer.
baselineEntries.when: ANC + FF+ selected · Any municipality (national backstory)
baselineEntries.basis: ANC and FF+ joined the GNU despite political differences. Campaign posters requesting a transfer personifies the awkward reversal.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: ANC and FF+ were named as participants in the national GNU in June 2024. The appointments included IFP’s Velenkosini Hlabisa at Cooperative Governance, PA’s Gayton McKenzie at Sport, Arts and Culture, and FF+’s Pieter Groenewald at Correctional Services. This does not establish a local coalition.

baselineEntries.text: IFP + PA: Hlabisa tries to cooperate. Gayton appeals to the referee.
baselineEntries.when: IFP + PA selected · Any municipality (national backstory)
baselineEntries.basis: IFP’s Hlabisa received Cooperative Governance while PA’s McKenzie received Sport. The joke combines the portfolio names with fictional personalities.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: IFP and PA were named as participants in the national GNU in June 2024. The appointments included IFP’s Velenkosini Hlabisa at Cooperative Governance, PA’s Gayton McKenzie at Sport, Arts and Culture, and FF+’s Pieter Groenewald at Correctional Services. This does not establish a local coalition.

baselineEntries.text: IFP + FF+: left to stop the ANC. Came home with GNU lanyards.
baselineEntries.when: IFP + FF+ selected · Any municipality (national backstory)
baselineEntries.basis: Both joined the anti-ANC Charter, then the ANC-inclusive GNU. The lanyards represent their new government access.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: IFP and FF+ were named as participants in the national GNU in June 2024. The appointments included IFP’s Velenkosini Hlabisa at Cooperative Governance, PA’s Gayton McKenzie at Sport, Arts and Culture, and FF+’s Pieter Groenewald at Correctional Services. IFP and FF+ had also joined the August 2023 Charter talks aimed at replacing the ANC government. This does not establish a local coalition.

baselineEntries.text: PA + FF+: Sport meets Correctional Services. Extra time has two meanings.
baselineEntries.when: PA + FF+ selected · Any municipality (national backstory)
baselineEntries.basis: PA received Sport and FF+ Correctional Services in 2024. Extra time means both more play in sport and a longer prison term.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.note: Extra time is a wordplay on two portfolios; it must not imply coalition partners have committed crimes.
baselineEntries.fact: PA and FF+ were named as participants in the national GNU in June 2024. The appointments included IFP’s Velenkosini Hlabisa at Cooperative Governance, PA’s Gayton McKenzie at Sport, Arts and Culture, and FF+’s Pieter Groenewald at Correctional Services. This does not establish a local coalition.

baselineEntries.text: IFP + ActionSA: the old pact is back. Please ignore where everyone went afterwards.
baselineEntries.when: IFP + ActionSA selected · Any municipality (national backstory)
baselineEntries.basis: Both joined the Charter; IFP later joined the GNU while ActionSA’s Tshwane mayor relied on ANC/EFF support. Their later choices complicate the old pact.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: IFP and ActionSA participated in the August 2023 Multi-Party Charter talks, aimed at replacing the ANC government and keeping the EFF out. In 2024, IFP joined the ANC-inclusive GNU, while ActionSA’s Nasiphi Moya became Tshwane mayor with ANC and EFF support. These later national and local choices explain the reunion joke; they do not establish a pact in this municipality.

baselineEntries.text: FF+ + ActionSA: the anti-ANC pact has some awkward post-election photos.
baselineEntries.when: FF+ + ActionSA selected · Any municipality (national backstory)
baselineEntries.basis: Both joined an anti-ANC pact, then cooperated with ANC in different settings. The awkward photos are fictional shorthand for those later alignments.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: FF+ and ActionSA participated in the August 2023 Multi-Party Charter talks, aimed at replacing the ANC government and keeping the EFF out. In 2024, FF+ joined the ANC-inclusive GNU, while ActionSA’s Nasiphi Moya became Tshwane mayor with ANC and EFF support. These later national and local choices explain the reunion joke; they do not establish a pact in this municipality.

baselineEntries.text: EFF + MK: please check which side Floyd was on when that photo was taken.
baselineEntries.when: EFF + MK selected · Any municipality (national backstory)
baselineEntries.basis: Shivambu left EFF for MK in August 2024. A photo taken before versus after the move would show a different affiliation.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: EFF deputy president Floyd Shivambu left for MK in August 2024. MK named him National Organiser on 22 August. This dated leadership transfer is a backstory, not his current role or proof of a local alliance.

baselineEntries.text: EFF + IFP: reunited. Please don’t ask who gets uMhlathuze.
baselineEntries.when: EFF + IFP selected · Any municipality (national backstory)
baselineEntries.basis: Their January 2023 breakup involved negotiations over the uMhlathuze mayoralty. The reunion joke avoids reopening that dispute.
baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: IFP and EFF accounts describe the end of their cooperation in January 2023. The IFP said it declined an EFF request to lead uMhlathuze; the EFF announced the withdrawal of support. Their accounts of responsibility differed. National negotiations concerned particular councils, not every municipality.

sources.label: IFP account of coalition talks · January 2023

baselineEntries.text: EFF + FF+: one letter apart. Several planets away.
baselineEntries.when: EFF + FF+ selected · Any municipality (national backstory) · Newly completed public red line gets priority.

baselineEntries.text: MK + FF+: even agreeing to disagree may need a recess.
baselineEntries.when: MK + FF+ selected · Any municipality (national backstory) · Newly completed public red line gets priority.

baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.note: Policy disagreement is weaker than a refusal to negotiate; retain that distinction.
baselineEntries.fact: At the FF+ campaign launch in May 2026, Corné Mulder said his party did not align with MK, EFF and ANC policies, while expressing openness to coalition government. Policy disagreement is not the same as an unconditional refusal to negotiate.

baselineEntries.text: IFP + MK: one won the biggest bloc, the other got the keys. Lovely reunion.

baselineEntries.meaning: The joke applies this dated political history to your fictional deal. It does not report a current alliance or a real private conversation.
baselineEntries.fact: MK won the largest share in KwaZulu-Natal in 2024 without an outright majority. IFP’s Thami Ntuli became premier after a 41–39 legislature vote. This provincial rivalry is not proof of a municipal agreement or a permanent ban on cooperation.

A truce at the family braai.

Two logos, one pothole.

The microphone is not a portfolio.
DA and PA hold a joint briefing. Both want the last word. {actor} takes its seats and leaves the other party with the microphone.

baselineEntries.basis: DA and PA both joined the GNU. Interrupting each other is a fictional personality joke, not a sourced incident.

DA and PA put the local deal in writing. Even the press conference has a speaking order. Everyone stays.

The reunion needs a referee.
ANC and EFF agree to leave the old Ekurhuleni arguments outside. The arguments get their own visitor passes. {actor} leaves the deal.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing ANC + EFF. Ekurhuleni.
baselineEntries.basis: ANC and EFF’s Ekurhuleni arrangement faced a disrupted council sitting and threatened breakup in 2024. The relationship metaphor exaggerates that friction.

baselineEntries.fact: ANC and EFF governed together in Ekurhuleni in 2023–2024. In March 2024, ANC representatives publicly threatened to end the arrangement after a disrupted council sitting. Their explanations were political claims, not an agreed account of blame.

baselineEntries.text:
The minutes survive the meeting.
ANC and EFF agree on the agenda and finish it. The minute-taker asks them to repeat that for the record. Everyone stays.

baselineEntries.text:
The music stops. Who’s mayor?
ANC and EFF discuss the Bay’s seating plan. Someone moves the mayoral chair while the others are talking. {actor} walks out.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing ANC + EFF. Nelson Mandela Bay.
baselineEntries.basis: ANC and EFF helped replace Nelson Mandela Bay’s DA mayor with Northern Alliance’s Gary van Niekerk in 2023. Their votes put a third party in the top job.
baselineEntries.meaning: An invented breakdown riffing on this history. {actor} is chosen equally from the relevant selected parties; the script does not assign historical blame.
baselineEntries.outcome: The chosen party leaves with all its seats. Compare remaining support with the original majority target.
baselineEntries.fact: In May 2023, a coalition including ANC and EFF helped replace DA mayor Retief Odendaal with Gary van Niekerk of the Northern Alliance. Van Niekerk had been council speaker. This is a historical leadership change, not today’s coalition map.

baselineEntries.text:
Same mayor after lunch.
ANC and EFF agree to finish the water-services agenda before discussing the mayoral chain. The chairs stay exactly where they are.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing ANC + EFF. Nelson Mandela Bay.

baselineEntries.text:
The lagoon is the calm part.
ANC and PA promise a quiet Knysna meeting. Then the appointments item arrives. {actor} leaves before anyone reaches “any other business”.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing ANC + PA. Knysna.
baselineEntries.basis: PA withdrew from Knysna’s ANC-led coalition in 2023. The oyster reference is a local Knysna image for a delicate reunion.

baselineEntries.outcome: The chosen party leaves with all its seats. Compare remaining support with the original majority target.
baselineEntries.note: Knysna oysters are recognisable locally, but “carefully, and on ice” may be a thin political punchline.
baselineEntries.fact: In September 2023, PA councillors resigned from Knysna’s mayoral committee and the party announced its withdrawal from the ANC-led coalition. The PA linked its decision to senior appointments; that was its stated reason.

baselineEntries.text:
An agreement with a view.
ANC and PA agree on the appointments process before debating office views. The meeting ends with all partners still in the room.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing ANC + PA. Knysna.

baselineEntries.text:
Confidence has left the building.
ANC and EFF agree that confidence is essential. They disagree on who should have it. {actor} leaves the Durban deal.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing ANC + EFF. eThekwini.
baselineEntries.basis: EFF votes helped defeat a no-confidence motion against ANC mayor Kaunda in 2023. It contrasts revolutionary rhetoric with supporting an ANC officeholder.

baselineEntries.outcome: The chosen party leaves with all its seats. Compare remaining support with the original majority target.
baselineEntries.fact: EFF councillors voted against a no-confidence motion targeting ANC mayor Mxolisi Kaunda in February 2023. The motion failed. Supporting a mayor in that vote did not by itself establish a formal coalition agreement.

baselineEntries.text:
A point of agreement.
ANC and EFF come prepared for a point of order. They accidentally find a point of agreement. Everyone stays for the actual agenda.

Please see the original agreement.
DA and ActionSA bring different versions of the old pact to the meeting. Both files are called FINAL. {actor} leaves before FINAL_v3 appears.

DA and ActionSA agree on a local plan. They even sign the same version. The printer gets a standing ovation.

That was not one of the issues.
ANC and ActionSA agree to take things issue by issue. Item two turns out to be whether item one counted. {actor} leaves the deal.

It works for this agenda item.
ANC and ActionSA agree on the water-repair plan. Nobody updates their relationship status. Everyone stays for the vote.

baselineEntries.text:
Who is steering this thing?
ANC and Al Jama-ah both bring a steering wheel to the mayoral office. There is only one chair. {actor} leaves before the driving lesson.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing ANC + Al Jama-ah. Johannesburg.
baselineEntries.basis: Al Jama-ah supplied Joburg’s mayor in the broader ANC-backed unity coalition. The junior partner getting the main bedroom means a small party taking the top office.
baselineEntries.meaning: An invented breakdown riffing on this history. {actor} is chosen equally from the relevant selected parties; the script does not assign historical blame.
baselineEntries.outcome: The chosen party leaves with all its seats. Compare remaining support with the original majority target.
baselineEntries.fact: Al Jama-ah’s Thapelo Amad became Johannesburg mayor in January 2023 under the Government of Local Unity, which included the ANC and EFF. The city’s annual report records his resignation in April 2023.

baselineEntries.text:
The chain comes with a manual.
ANC and Al Jama-ah agree who leads and who supports. The mayoral chain comes with a work plan this time. Everyone stays.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing ANC + Al Jama-ah. Johannesburg.

The office is bigger than the caucus.
ANC and COPE finish the seating plan. Then they notice the mayoral office is bigger than the negotiation room. {actor} reopens the deal by leaving it.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing ANC + COPE. Tshwane.
baselineEntries.basis: ANC and EFF helped elect COPE’s Makwarela as Tshwane mayor in February 2023. A very small party obtained the senior role.

baselineEntries.fact: Tshwane elected COPE’s Murunwa Makwarela mayor on 28 February 2023. ATM nominated him, with ANC and EFF support. This records that election, not an enduring agreement between all those parties.

baselineEntries.text:
One chair, agreed occupant.
ANC and COPE decide who wears the chain before ordering the nameplate. The engraver is stunned. All your seats stay.

baselineEntries.text:
Compromise candidate, uncompromising partners.
ANC and EFF agree neither should take the top job. Both insist on choosing who does. {actor} leaves with the shortlist.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing ANC + EFF. Tshwane.
baselineEntries.basis: ANC and EFF supported a COPE mayor in Tshwane in 2023. They supplied support while another party got the mayoralty.
baselineEntries.meaning: An invented breakdown riffing on this history. {actor} is chosen equally from the relevant selected parties; the script does not assign historical blame.
baselineEntries.outcome: The chosen party leaves with all its seats. Compare remaining support with the original majority target.
baselineEntries.fact: ANC and EFF supported COPE’s Murunwa Makwarela in Tshwane’s February 2023 mayoral election. He defeated the DA’s Cilliers Brink by 112 votes to 101. Voting together did not itself establish a permanent coalition.

baselineEntries.text:
A candidate everyone can pronounce.
ANC and EFF settle the nomination before the Speaker finishes calling the meeting to order. All your partners stay. The microphones look underemployed.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing ANC + EFF. Tshwane.

baselineEntries.text:
Return ticket. Terms apply.
DA and EFF agree on a mayor, then disagree whether support included the return journey. {actor} leaves. The chair is still warm.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing DA + EFF. Ekurhuleni.
baselineEntries.basis: EFF votes helped return DA mayor Tania Campbell to office in November 2022. It was voting support, not proof of a formal DA–EFF coalition.
baselineEntries.meaning: An invented breakdown riffing on this history. {actor} is chosen equally from the relevant selected parties; the script does not assign historical blame.
baselineEntries.outcome: The chosen party leaves with all its seats. Compare remaining support with the original majority target.
baselineEntries.fact: After ANC–EFF talks failed, EFF votes helped return DA mayor Tania Campbell to office on 8 November 2022, two weeks after her removal. This was voting support for a minority administration, not proof of a formal DA–EFF coalition.

baselineEntries.text:
Back by unexpected demand.
DA and EFF agree to keep the deal going for today’s work. Nobody calls it a friendship. Everyone stays anyway.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing DA + EFF. Ekurhuleni.

baselineEntries.text:
The deputy has notes.
ANC and ABC agree on the mayoral team. The deputy’s job description arrives with track changes and an exit clause. {actor} uses the exit.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing ANC + ABC. eThekwini.
baselineEntries.basis: ANC brought the motion that removed ABC’s Philani Mavundla as eThekwini deputy mayor in 2022. Ejector seat means a precarious coalition post.
baselineEntries.meaning: An invented breakdown riffing on this history. {actor} is chosen equally from the relevant selected parties; the script does not assign historical blame.
baselineEntries.outcome: The chosen party leaves with all its seats. Compare remaining support with the original majority target.
baselineEntries.fact: ABC leader Philani Mavundla lost his eThekwini executive-committee position and deputy mayoralty in December 2022. The ANC brought the removal motion; the council minutes record ANC and EFF votes in favour.

baselineEntries.text:
Deputy, not temporary.
ANC and ABC settle the deputy’s role before the first meeting. The nameplate can finally be screwed in. Nobody leaves.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing ANC + ABC. eThekwini.
baselineEntries.basis: ANC brought the motion that removed ABC’s Philani Mavundla as eThekwini deputy mayor in 2022. Ejector seat means a precarious coalition post.

baselineEntries.text:
Two posters. One promise.
DA and IFP promise not to step on each other’s toes. Both book the same campaign lamppost. {actor} leaves over the fine print.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing DA + IFP. eThekwini.
baselineEntries.basis: DA and IFP agreed not to compete with each other in a particular eThekwini by-election. Cooperation meant one party standing aside in that ward.
baselineEntries.meaning: An invented breakdown riffing on this history. {actor} is chosen equally from the relevant selected parties; the script does not assign historical blame.
baselineEntries.outcome: The chosen party leaves with all its seats. Compare remaining support with the original majority target.
baselineEntries.fact: Ahead of eThekwini’s December 2022 ward 99 by-election, the DA and IFP arranged not to compete against each other there. The IFP won the ward from the ANC. A ward-level electoral arrangement is not a citywide governing coalition.

baselineEntries.text:
After you, coalition partner.
DA and IFP agree who gets this turn. One campaign loudspeaker switches off voluntarily. All your councillors stay.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing DA + IFP. eThekwini.
baselineEntries.basis: DA and IFP agreed not to compete with each other in a particular eThekwini by-election. Cooperation meant one party standing aside in that ward.

baselineEntries.text:
Seven parties, one diary.
DA and ACDP revisit Cape Town’s coalition prequel. The meeting invitation needs seven approvals. {actor} leaves before a date is found.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing DA + ACDP. Cape Town.
baselineEntries.basis: ACDP joined Cape Town’s seven-party coalition in 2006. The prayer is a wordplay on the party’s Christian identity, not a claim about a religious event.

baselineEntries.fact: In 2006, the DA assembled a seven-party Cape Town coalition including the ACDP, FF+ and UDM. Helen Zille became mayor and ACDP councillor Andrew Arnolds became deputy mayor.

baselineEntries.text:
The prequel gets a happy ending.
DA and ACDP remember how many calls the old deal took. They answer on the first ring this time. Everyone stays.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing DA + ACDP. Cape Town.

baselineEntries.text:
The prequel has a director’s cut.
DA and FF+ retell the 2006 coalition story. Each has a different main character. {actor} walks out before the credits.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing DA + FF+. Cape Town.
baselineEntries.basis: FF+ joined that seven-party Cape Town coalition and supplied the Speaker. The bell stands for control of debate.

baselineEntries.fact: The FF+ joined Cape Town’s DA-led seven-party coalition in 2006. Its councillor Dirk Smit became speaker. This historical coalition predates the DA’s later outright city majorities.

baselineEntries.text:
Roll the original credits.
DA and FF+ agree that every partner gets a credit in the coalition story. Then they get through the actual council agenda. Everyone stays.

baselineEntries.text:
The old save file loads.
The DA caucus argues over who gets credit for the city’s coalition origin story. Half of {actor}’s delegation withholds support until the credits are rewritten.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing DA. Cape Town.
baselineEntries.basis: The DA needed six partners to govern Cape Town in 2006. The solo-career joke teases later narratives of governing alone.

The DA caucus remembers that a majority once required six partners and a lot of phone calls. Everyone agrees to finish the work plan. All seats stay.

baselineEntries.text:
The ballot did not read the memo.
ANC and DA announce that everyone knows the plan. The plan asks for clarification. {actor} leaves before the Speaker gets to nominations.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing ANC + DA. Mangaung.
baselineEntries.basis: Some ANC councillors backed DA’s Maryke Davies for Mangaung Speaker against their party’s choice in 2023. Opposition here came from within the ANC.

The caucus memo gets a reply-all.
The ANC caucus sends out one instruction. The replies contain two alternative instructions. Half of {actor}’s delegation withholds support.

baselineEntries.basis: ANC councillors split over Mangaung’s Speaker vote. A numerical majority did not guarantee internal agreement.

baselineEntries.text:
The nameplate has been recalled.
The ANC caucus agrees it wants change. It cannot agree whose office should change first. Half of {actor}’s delegation withholds support.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing ANC. Buffalo City.
baselineEntries.basis: ANC recalled its own Buffalo City mayor in 2023. The opposition did not need to trigger that leadership change.

baselineEntries.fact: The ANC recalled Buffalo City mayor Xola Pakati in March 2023. Princess Faku replaced him on 23 March, winning 62 votes to the DA candidate’s 22. The ANC held a majority; this was an internal leadership change, not a coalition collapse.

baselineEntries.text:
Same team after the reshuffle.
The ANC caucus settles the leadership question and keeps the service plan. The nameplate changes; your support does not. All seats stay.

The keyring is up for negotiation.
ANC and ATM agree on the mayoral office, then disagree on who keeps the spare keys. {actor} leaves before the handover.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing ANC + ATM. Mogale City.
baselineEntries.basis: ATM’s Danny Thupane became mayor under an ATM–ANC–EFF arrangement in Mogale City in 2023. Executive package means the top office.

baselineEntries.fact: Mogale City elected ATM’s Danny Thupane mayor in April 2023, replacing the DA-led administration. The municipality named ATM, ANC and EFF as participants in the new Government of Local Unity.

baselineEntries.text:
Small party, signed mandate.
ANC and ATM put the mayor’s duties in writing. The keys and the responsibility go to the same person. Everyone stays.

The three-way call drops.
ANC and EFF arrange a three-way leadership call. Everyone talks; nobody knows who is chairing. {actor} leaves the deal and the call.

baselineEntries.basis: ANC and EFF joined an arrangement that gave Mogale’s mayoralty to ATM. Boss is comic shorthand for the mayor, not a legal chain of command between parties.

The small print has a caucus.
ANC and PA draft the Vaal deal. The smaller partners arrive with amendments to the amendments. {actor} leaves before the appendix is finished.

baselineEntries.basis: After ANC lost its outright majority, PA and local parties helped it govern Emfuleni. Terms and conditions means having to bargain with partners.

baselineEntries.text:
Small seat count. Large invoice of demands.
ANC and AIC agree every partner matters. Then they discuss exactly how much. {actor} leaves with its list of conditions.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing ANC + AIC. Rustenburg.
baselineEntries.basis: AIC and Arona helped ANC reach a majority in Rustenburg after 2021. Platinum references the area; no actual monetary demand is alleged.

baselineEntries.fact: After the 2021 election, Rustenburg’s ANC formed a governing arrangement with the AIC and local party Arona. MISTRA records how small-party support helped the ANC reach a council majority.

The top-up has terms.
ANC and PA agree on the majority. The final two lines of the agreement take longer than the first twenty. {actor} leaves over the wording.

baselineEntries.basis: ANC was one seat short of a majority in JB Marks; PA’s two seats supplied the support. Expensive means political bargaining power, not a proven payment.
