The ink has not dried.
ANC and PA sign the Ditsobotla deal. Someone asks about an appointment before the pens are capped. {actor} leaves. The laminator remains unplugged.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing ANC + PA. Ditsobotla.
baselineEntries.basis: A new PA mayor announced her resignation within hours in 2023. The Home Affairs queue is an exaggerated familiar comparison, not measured timing.

Head office has entered the chat.
ANC and EFF complete the local handshake. A national office calls to ask who authorised the handshake. {actor} leaves to “consult”.

baselineEntries.basis: An EFF mayor elected with ANC support resigned after EFF national leadership objected. Local chemistry is also a nod to Sasolburg’s industrial identity.

baselineEntries.fact: EFF mayor Selloane Motjeane resigned in November 2021 after her party’s national leadership objected to her election with ANC support. The DA’s Jeff Zwane succeeded her in December. Local support and national instructions had diverged.

The mayoral chain needs an extension.
ANC and AIC agree to share responsibility. Both pull the mayoral chain in their direction. {actor} lets go and leaves the deal.

baselineEntries.basis: AIC’s Jack Malindi became mayor with ANC and ATM support in 2023. The chain stands for a large role obtained by a small party.

The chain stays in one piece.

Oversight needs its own oversight.
MAP16 and EFF agree that somebody must check the work. They disagree about who checks the checker. {actor} leaves before the first report.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing MAP16 + EFF. Maluti a Phofung.
baselineEntries.basis: EFF agreed to oversee public accounts while supporting MAP16’s leadership rather than formally co-governing. The audit joke is about oversight within a support arrangement.

baselineEntries.text:
The sweet deal turns sticky.
IFP and Team Sugar agree to give each other space. Both turn up with a campaign gazebo for the same corner. {actor} packs up and leaves.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing IFP + TSSA. Newcastle.
baselineEntries.basis: IFP stood aside for Team Sugar in one Newcastle by-election in 2023. Sweetness is a pun on Team Sugar’s name.

baselineEntries.outcome: The chosen party leaves with all its seats. Compare remaining support with the original majority target.
baselineEntries.note: The sweet-name pun is easy to understand but fairly mild; the actual ward arrangement is more interesting than the punchline.
baselineEntries.fact: In February 2023, the IFP agreed not to contest Newcastle’s ward 31 by-election and to support coalition partner Team Sugar South Africa. The partners publicly confirmed the arrangement and denied that it had been forced by threats.

One gazebo. Shared shade.

Both want to be captain.

Heads, we need another meeting.

baselineEntries.basis: EFF left the original DA-led arrangement; prolonged council disputes preceded dissolution in 2024. The drama outliving the council is a compressed timeline joke.

baselineEntries.text:
The office swap hits a snag.
DA and NCM agree it is time to swap offices. Both want to keep the chair with good back support. {actor} leaves before moving day.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing DA + NCM. NAMA KHOI.
baselineEntries.basis: DA and NCM swapped mayor and Speaker positions under an agreed rotation in July 2024. Musical chairs was planned rather than a surprise breakup.

Musical chairs, as scheduled.
DA and NCM swap roles exactly as agreed. Even the pot plants make it to the right offices. Everyone stays in the deal.

The deputy chair squeaks.
DA and UDM discuss who sits where. The deputy mayor’s chair makes a noise suspiciously like “remember 2017?” {actor} leaves the deal.
baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing DA + UDM. Nelson Mandela Bay.
baselineEntries.basis: UDM deputy mayor Mongameli Bobani was removed in 2017 amid a dispute with DA partners. Abandonment issues personifies the deputy’s chair.

The reunion needs another appendix.
DA and FF+ reopen the George agreement. The appendices have developed their own appendices. {actor} leaves before the stapler gives up.

DA and FF+ sign the reunion agreement and file the old argument under lessons learned. Everyone stays. The stapler survives.

The portfolio comes with paperwork.

baselineEntries.when: Test a majority containing DA + ACDP. George.
baselineEntries.basis: ACDP received George’s Corporate Services portfolio under a 2025 agreement. Prayer is a pun on the Christian party’s identity; the portfolio is the real hook.

A GOOD day for the minutes.
DA and GOOD update the seating chart and agree on the water-services agenda. The meeting ends without another furniture rearrangement.

The sea view is under negotiation.

baselineEntries.basis: PDC left a DA-led arrangement; its councillor became mayor in an ANC-aligned arrangement in 2024. The hotel suite is a Plett-flavoured office metaphor.

DA and PDC agree the town needs a work plan before an office tour. Everyone stays. The sea remains entirely unimpressed.

Checkout time for the coalition.
ANC and PA book the coalition’s future. One reads the booking as long-term, the other as a weekend stay. {actor} checks out with its seats.

baselineEntries.basis: ANC, PA and others formed a Bitou arrangement in February 2024 that changed again later that year. Checkout compares coalition turnover with a holiday stay.

ANC and PA agree the work needs more than a weekend. Everyone stays to finish the plan. Nobody asks for an early checkout.

The nameplate is still warm.

baselineEntries.text:
The breakaway press conference.
Two councillors launch a breakaway. The new logo is ready. The explanation is still loading.
baselineEntries.when: Any majority.
baselineEntries.basis: Invented council satire; no specific historical incident.
baselineEntries.meaning: New parties announcing themselves with branding before a clear political explanation.
baselineEntries.note: Accuracy: the story always says “Two councillors”, even if a hypothetical one-seat deal can only lose one.
baselineEntries.outcome: Lose two seats, capped at the seats in the deal.

baselineEntries.text:
“Consulting our structures.”
One councillor withholds support to consult their structures. The structures appear to be a coffee shop.
baselineEntries.when: Any majority.
baselineEntries.basis: Invented council satire; no specific historical incident.
baselineEntries.meaning: “Consulting our structures” is familiar party language for referring a decision back to internal bodies. The coffee-shop reveal mocks that formality.
baselineEntries.outcome: Lose one seat.

baselineEntries.text:
The blue-light delay.
One councillor misses the meeting. Their convoy is apparently stuck behind a very determined delivery scooter.
baselineEntries.when: Any majority.
baselineEntries.basis: Invented council satire; no specific historical incident.
baselineEntries.meaning: Blue-light convoys signify VIP travel. An ordinary delivery scooter defeating one reverses the status hierarchy.
baselineEntries.outcome: One seat is unavailable.

baselineEntries.text:
Two ribbon cuttings. One council.
Two councillors choose a photo opportunity over the council meeting. The ribbon is cut. Your numbers are too.
baselineEntries.when: Any majority.
baselineEntries.basis: Invented council satire; no specific historical incident.
baselineEntries.meaning: Politicians favouring ribbon-cutting publicity over routine council work. “Your numbers are too” turns cutting a ribbon into losing votes.
baselineEntries.note: Accuracy: the story says two councillors even in the one-seat edge case.
baselineEntries.outcome: Lose two seats, capped at the seats in the deal.

baselineEntries.text:
Everyone wants to chair something.
Half the {party} delegation withholds support after a committee-chair argument. Everyone insists this is about service delivery.
baselineEntries.when: Any majority.
baselineEntries.basis: Invented council satire; no specific historical incident.
baselineEntries.meaning: A fight over committee positions is dressed up as concern for service delivery. No particular real dispute is alleged.
baselineEntries.outcome: A randomly selected party withholds half its seats, rounded up.

baselineEntries.text:
Madam Speaker calls tea.
The argument is paused for tea. By the time the biscuits arrive, everyone has forgotten who threatened to leave.
baselineEntries.when: Any majority.
baselineEntries.basis: Invented council satire; no specific historical incident.
baselineEntries.meaning: A parliamentary tea break and biscuits deflate a grand political confrontation.
baselineEntries.outcome: No seats lost.

baselineEntries.text:
The budget actually passes.

baselineEntries.text: DA: the ANC was the problem. Until it had vacancies.
baselineEntries.when: Not displayed. Proposed first-pick alternative.
baselineEntries.basis: The DA campaigned against ANC rule, including its 2024 Rescue Plan, then joined the ANC-inclusive GNU.
baselineEntries.meaning: The DA opposed ANC rule, then took roles in the ANC-inclusive GNU. The punchline cheekily recasts that reversal as job hunting.
baselineEntries.note: Suggested in chat; not applied to the game. A sharper opportunism joke, not evidence of a private motive.
baselineEntries.fact: The DA campaigned under its Rescue Plan for South Africa in 2024, positioning itself against ANC rule. It joined the ANC and other parties in the national GNU in June 2024. Cooperation nationally does not establish a local coalition.

baselineEntries.text: EFF: wanted to take power. MK took the deputy.
baselineEntries.when: Not displayed. Proposed first-pick alternative.
baselineEntries.basis: Floyd Shivambu, then EFF deputy president, left for MK in August 2024.
baselineEntries.meaning: The EFF aimed to win government power; instead, its deputy president moved to rival MK. It is a reversal of who gained from whom.
baselineEntries.note: Suggested in chat; not applied. Clearer about Shivambu’s move; “took” does not mean coercion.
baselineEntries.fact: EFF deputy president Floyd Shivambu left for MK in August 2024. MK named him National Organiser on 22 August. This describes that transfer, not his subsequent positions.

baselineEntries.text: IFP: got the KZN premier’s chair. It came with three back-seat drivers.
baselineEntries.when: Not displayed. Proposed first-pick alternative.
baselineEntries.basis: Thami Ntuli became KZN premier in June 2024 by 41 votes to 39, with ANC, DA and NFP support alongside IFP.
baselineEntries.meaning: The IFP held the premiership while three coalition partners also wanted a say.
baselineEntries.note: The three partners are ANC, DA and NFP. Back-seat driving exaggerates their influence; it does not establish a legal veto.
baselineEntries.fact: The IFP’s Thami Ntuli won the June 2024 premiership vote in the KwaZulu-Natal legislature, 41–39, after negotiations involving the IFP, ANC, DA and NFP. This is provincial history, not a municipal pact.

baselineEntries.meaning: The premier got the top office but had to share political power with three partners.
baselineEntries.note: The roommates are ANC, DA and NFP. A simple metaphor for having to share power.
baselineEntries.fact: The IFP’s Thami Ntuli won the June 2024 premiership vote in the KwaZulu-Natal legislature, 41–39, after negotiations involving the IFP, ANC, DA and NFP. This is provincial history, not a municipal pact.

baselineEntries.meaning: Willingness to cooperate ran into a dispute over who would control uMhlathuze’s mayoralty.
baselineEntries.note: This is the uMhlathuze/IFP–EFF dispute, not the KZN premiership story.
baselineEntries.fact: IFP and EFF accounts describe an end to their cooperation in January 2023. The IFP said it had refused an EFF request to lead uMhlathuze; the EFF announced the withdrawal of support. Their explanations of responsibility differed.

changes.reason: Spell out meeting minutes so the contrast works without council terminology.

changes.oldText: No partners to blame. The caucus will have to improvise.
changes.newText: No coalition partners to blame. Your own councillors will have to improvise.
changes.meaning: A party governing alone has to invent another excuse when things go wrong.
changes.reason: Replace caucus with own councillors and identify the absent coalition partners.

changes.oldText: One party. The factions have requested separate microphones.
changes.newText: One party. Still arguing over who gets the microphone.
changes.meaning: Even one party can contain competing voices.
changes.reason: Make the internal disagreement visible without needing to know what factions are.

changes.oldText: A whole majority. The internal opposition is warming up.
changes.newText: A whole majority. Now watch the party argue with itself.
changes.meaning: Winning enough seats does not make everyone within the party agree.
changes.reason: Replace the abstract internal opposition with a recognisable argument.

changes.oldText: Nobody breathe near the smallest partner.
changes.newText: Even the smallest partner can bring this down. Handle with care.
changes.meaning: When every partner is pivotal, even the smallest needs careful handling.
changes.reason: Put the reason for the exaggerated caution into the joke; this only appears when every partner is pivotal.

changes.oldText: I’ll take the minutes. Someone else can take the credit.
changes.newText: I’ll take the meeting notes. Someone else can take the credit.
changes.meaning: The Speaker does the routine work while someone else claims the achievement.
changes.reason: Keep the take/take wordplay while spelling out meeting minutes.

changes.oldText: The big-tent deal.
changes.newText: The crowded table.
changes.meaning: Several parties share the bargaining table.
changes.reason: Use a visible scene instead of the political term big tent.

changes.oldText:
“Consulting our structures.”
One councillor withholds support to consult their structures. The structures appear to be a coffee shop.
changes.newText:
“We need to consult the party.”
One councillor withholds support for an urgent party consultation. The only person consulted so far is the barista.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: a supposedly urgent party consultation turns into a conversation with a barista.
changes.reason: Replace opaque party jargon with the plain excuse, then let the coffee shop supply the punchline.

changes.oldText:
The committee needs a committee.
Half the {party} delegation withholds support while councillors debate how to share committee roles. Madam Speaker asks who is chairing the discussion about chairs.
changes.newText:
The committee needs a committee.
Half the {party} councillors withhold support while everyone argues over who gets to lead the committees. They agree to form another committee to decide.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: an argument about committee leaders produces yet another committee.
changes.reason: Explain the leadership dispute directly and use unnecessary bureaucracy as the punchline.

changes.oldText:
The caucus has two group chats.
Half your caucus rebels. Both factions insist they are the real caucus. Both have made a new group icon.
changes.newText:
One party. Two group chats.
Half your party’s councillors refuse to back the deal. Both sides claim to speak for the whole party. Both have made a new group icon.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: a split within one party becomes rival group chats, each claiming to represent everyone.
changes.reason: Name the party split without requiring the term caucus. State whose support is withheld while keeping the competing group icons.

changes.oldText: Calling an urgent caucus…
changes.newText: Calling an urgent party meeting…
changes.meaning: The parties pause for an emergency discussion.
changes.reason: Use the everyday meaning of caucus in the loading line.

changes.oldText: ANC: eleven parties in the GNU. Still acting like it owns the remote.
changes.newText: ANC: eleven parties sharing a government. Still acting like it owns the remote.
changes.meaning: Eleven parties shared the 2024 unity government; the remote-control joke imagines the ANC still treating the shared household as its own.
changes.reason: Replaces the unexplained GNU acronym with the arrangement needed for the household joke.

changes.oldText: ANC: the GNU is a family meeting where everyone brought their own party.
changes.newText: ANC: unity government is a family meeting where everyone brought their own party.
changes.meaning: A government of several political parties becomes a crowded family gathering, with a second meaning for party.
changes.reason: Names unity government directly so the reader does not have to decode GNU.

changes.oldText: ANC: the family reunion now needs two sets of campaign posters.
changes.newText: ANC: ex-president Zuma backed MK. Now the family reunion needs two sets of campaign posters.
changes.meaning: Former ANC president Jacob Zuma backed a different party, so former political family members now campaign under different party banners.
changes.reason: Adds the missing former-president and party-change setup for the family-reunion metaphor.

changes.oldText: ANC: suspended the ex. Couldn’t cancel the comeback tour.
changes.newText: ANC: suspended ex-president Zuma for backing MK. Couldn’t cancel the comeback tour.
changes.meaning: The ANC suspended its former president after he supported MK; the comeback-tour metaphor describes his continuing political presence.
changes.reason: Identifies the ex and the reason for the suspension without requiring the backstory panel.

changes.oldText: DA: spent years opposing the ANC. Then asked for a desk.
changes.newText: DA: spent years opposing the ANC. Then asked for a desk in the same government.
changes.meaning: The DA moved from opposing ANC rule to working in the same national government, imagined as asking for office space.
changes.reason: Explains what the desk stands for while preserving the short office joke.

changes.oldText: DA: rescued South Africa straight into a meeting with the ANC.
changes.newText: DA: promised a rescue from ANC rule. The escape route led to a shared Cabinet.
changes.meaning: The DA campaigned against ANC rule with its Rescue Plan, then joined a national Cabinet with the ANC.
changes.reason: States the campaign promise and the resulting shared government, so rescue is not an unexplained campaign reference.

changes.oldText: DA: the anti-ANC speeches must make Cabinet tea breaks awkward.
changes.newText: DA: anti-ANC speeches hit differently when the ANC joins you for Cabinet tea.
changes.meaning: Former opponents became Cabinet colleagues; imagined tea-break small talk carries the awkwardness of their earlier campaign rhetoric.
changes.reason: Makes it explicit that the ANC is now sharing the Cabinet table with the DA.

changes.oldText: DA: Steenhuisen got Agriculture in 2024. Finally, common ground he could point at.
changes.newText: DA: Steenhuisen became Agriculture minister in 2024. Finally, common ground he could point at.
changes.meaning: John Steenhuisen’s 2024 Agriculture appointment supplies literal farmland for the political phrase common ground.
changes.reason: Identifies Agriculture as a ministerial appointment; the name no longer needs to do the explanatory work.

changes.oldText: DA: Steenhuisen got Agriculture. The coalition still needs manure management.
changes.newText: DA: Steenhuisen got the Agriculture ministry. The coalition still needs manure management.
changes.meaning: The Agriculture portfolio sets up an earthy metaphor for managing coalition disagreements.
changes.reason: Makes the ministry explicit while preserving the original punchline and tone.

changes.oldText: DA: those old EFF votes make an awkward footnote to the campaign speeches.
changes.newText: DA: EFF votes once helped it govern councils. Awkward footnote to the anti-EFF speeches.
changes.meaning: Past EFF voting support helped DA-led councils, creating a contrast with the DA’s later political opposition to EFF involvement in national government.
changes.reason: Explains what the old votes achieved and which speeches make them awkward; it does not label the support a formal coalition.

changes.oldText: DA: red lines. Previously available in a more flexible municipal edition.
changes.newText: DA: accepted EFF council votes, opposed EFF Cabinet seats. Red lines with a municipal setting.
changes.meaning: The DA accepted issue-by-issue EFF support in councils but later opposed EFF inclusion in the national executive; the imaginary setting changes the red-line policy by level of government.
changes.reason: Supplies the two dated positions behind the red-lines joke instead of assuming the reader knows them.

changes.oldText: EFF: even the dress code wants the floor.
changes.newText: EFF: red overalls in Parliament. Even the dress code wants a speaking slot.
changes.meaning: The EFF’s recognisable parliamentary clothing is personified as another participant demanding to speak.
changes.reason: Names the clothing and setting and replaces the parliamentary idiom wants the floor with a speaking slot.

changes.oldText: EFF: business casual was apparently counter-revolutionary.
changes.newText: EFF: wore red overalls to Parliament. Business casual was apparently counter-revolutionary.
changes.meaning: Red workers’ overalls stand in comic contrast to conventional office clothing, with revolutionary language applied to a dress-code choice.
changes.reason: Adds the clothing choice that makes the business-casual punchline understandable.

changes.oldText: EFF: the DA’s municipal situationship. Don’t tag them in photos.
changes.newText: EFF: helped DA councils govern without joining the coalition. Don’t tag them in photos.
changes.meaning: EFF support helped DA-led councils without a formal governing coalition, likened to a relationship that avoids public couple photos.
changes.reason: Explains the support-without-membership arrangement and removes reliance on the slang situationship.

changes.oldText: EFF: revolutionary principles. Municipal terms and conditions apply.
changes.newText: EFF: helped the DA govern councils. Revolutionary principles, municipal terms and conditions apply.
changes.meaning: EFF support for DA-led councils is contrasted with its revolutionary political persona, using the language of contractual exceptions.
changes.reason: Adds the municipal cooperation that the original terms-and-conditions line left unstated.

changes.oldText: MK: the ANC’s greatest hits, with the original lead singer.
changes.newText: MK: the ANC’s greatest hits, with ex-president Zuma back on lead vocals.
changes.meaning: Former ANC president Jacob Zuma leading a new party is likened to a familiar singer returning with a different band.
changes.reason: Identifies the familiar singer and avoids making the reader infer which former ANC figure the joke means.

changes.oldText: MK: recruited Floyd Shivambu. The EFF got a forwarding address.
changes.newText: MK: recruited the EFF’s deputy, Floyd Shivambu. The EFF got a forwarding address.
changes.meaning: Floyd Shivambu moved from EFF deputy president to MK in 2024, imagined as leaving a forwarding address with his former party.
changes.reason: Identifies Shivambu’s previous role, which supplies the missing reason the EFF appears in the punchline.

changes.oldText: MK: won the biggest slice of KZN. Watched someone else cut the cake.
changes.newText: MK: most seats in KwaZulu-Natal. Its rivals pooled theirs and took the cake.
changes.meaning: MK was the largest party in the provincial legislature, but a grouping of other parties had enough votes to elect a different premier.
changes.reason: Expands the province name, identifies the slices as seats, and explains how other parties could prevail.

changes.oldText: MK: first in KZN. Then the other parties started adding.
changes.newText: MK: most seats in KwaZulu-Natal, but no majority. Then the other parties started adding.
changes.meaning: Having more seats than each other party individually did not give MK a majority; other parties could combine their votes.
changes.reason: States the missing distinction between the largest party and an outright majority before the arithmetic punchline.

changes.oldText: IFP: got the KZN keys. The coalition partners kept the spare set.
changes.newText: IFP: got the KwaZulu-Natal premier’s office. The coalition partners kept the spare keys.
changes.meaning: The IFP secured the premiership with other parties’ support, imagined as occupying an office to which coalition partners also hold keys.
changes.reason: Identifies the office and province instead of leaving KZN keys unexplained.

changes.oldText: IFP: that premier vote was too tight for a tea break.
changes.newText: IFP: won KZN’s premier vote 41–39. Too tight for a tea break.
changes.meaning: The 41–39 election of the IFP premier was close enough to inspire a joke about everyone needing to stay for the vote.
changes.reason: Supplies the close margin that explains why a tea break would be risky.

changes.oldText: IFP: Hlabisa got Cooperative Governance. Even the job title is wishful thinking.
changes.newText: IFP: Hlabisa got the Cooperative Governance ministry. In a coalition, even the title is wishful thinking.
changes.meaning: Hlabisa’s ministerial portfolio literally includes cooperative governance, a phrase turned into a joke about the work required to keep coalition partners cooperating.
changes.reason: Identifies the ministry and makes the coalition-cooperation wordplay explicit.

changes.oldText: IFP: the EFF reunion needs a mediator and separate chairs.
changes.newText: IFP: after the EFF breakup, any reunion needs a mediator and separate chairs.
changes.meaning: IFP–EFF cooperation ended in 2023; a hypothetical reunion is imagined as an awkward meeting requiring distance and mediation.
changes.reason: States that a breakup preceded the hypothetical reunion, without assigning blame or inventing a later reunion.

changes.oldText: PA: Sport, Arts and Culture. The coalition already had enough drama.
changes.newText: PA: got the Sport, Arts and Culture ministry. The coalition already had enough drama.
changes.meaning: The PA’s ministerial portfolio includes the arts, while coalition disagreements provide another, comic meaning of drama.
changes.reason: Explains why the list of sport, arts and culture appears before the drama joke.

changes.oldText: PA: Gayton got Sport. Passing the microphone remains optional.
changes.newText: PA: Gayton McKenzie got the sports ministry. Passing the microphone remains optional.
changes.meaning: Gayton McKenzie’s sports portfolio supplies the idea of passing, applied to the microphone and his outspoken public persona.
changes.reason: Uses the full name and identifies the ministry so the reader need not recognise Gayton or the appointment in advance.

changes.oldText: PA: the Central Karoo wasn’t big enough for the opening speech.
changes.newText: PA: Gayton McKenzie became Central Karoo district mayor. His opening speech needed a bigger district.
changes.meaning: McKenzie’s district mayoralty supplies the setting for an obviously exaggerated joke about an outsized speaking presence.
changes.reason: Names the person and actual district role before the hyperbole; it does not present the exaggerated speech as a sourced incident.

changes.oldText: ActionSA said it offered PA two Joburg portfolios in 2023. Apparently flowers wouldn’t do.
changes.newText: ActionSA said it offered two Joburg mayoral committee posts to win PA back in 2023. Apparently flowers wouldn’t do.
changes.meaning: ActionSA described offering two executive committee positions to restore PA support, likened to a reconciliation attempt requiring more than flowers.
changes.reason: Preserves the source attribution and year, identifies the political posts and explains the attempt to win PA back that makes flowers relevant.

changes.oldText: FF+: the anti-ANC pact had a Cabinet-sized loophole.
changes.newText: FF+: pledged to replace the ANC, then joined it in government. Cabinet-sized loophole.
changes.meaning: FF+ participated in an agreement aimed at replacing ANC government and later entered the ANC-inclusive national government.
changes.reason: States the before-and-after contradiction instead of assuming the reader knows the pact and Cabinet appointment.

changes.oldText: FF+: opposed the ANC right up to the Cabinet parking bay.
changes.newText: FF+: opposed the ANC, then joined it in the Cabinet carpool.
changes.meaning: Former opponents ended up sharing national government, imagined as sharing a ride to Cabinet.
changes.reason: Makes the shared Cabinet arrangement explicit while retaining the parking-and-commuting metaphor.

changes.oldText: FF+: the plus apparently includes the ANC.
changes.newText: FF+: joined the ANC in government. So that’s what the plus was for.
changes.meaning: FF+ joining government with the ANC creates a joke about the plus sign in its name adding another party.
changes.reason: Adds the governing arrangement that gives the plus-sign wordplay its meaning.

changes.oldText: FF+: a small Cape Town caucus with a Speaker-sized volume control.
changes.newText: FF+: got the Speaker’s job in Cape Town. Small party, big volume control.
changes.meaning: A small party’s councillor became Cape Town Speaker, with the chairing role imagined as a volume control over a much larger council.
changes.reason: Replaces caucus jargon and makes the actual Speaker appointment explicit.

changes.oldText: FF+: why win Cape Town when you can get the bell that shuts everyone up?
changes.newText: FF+: why win Cape Town outright when you can get the Speaker’s bell that shuts everyone up?
changes.meaning: Securing the Speaker’s role can give a small party an important council position without winning an outright majority; the bell exaggerates the chair’s power to call for order.
changes.reason: Identifies the bell with the Speaker and distinguishes winning an outright majority from gaining an influential coalition role.

changes.oldText: ActionSA: Herman left the DA. The arguments followed him home.
changes.newText: ActionSA: founder Herman Mashaba left the DA. The arguments followed him home.
changes.meaning: ActionSA’s founder previously belonged to the DA; the joke imagines the old political disagreements following him into his new party.
changes.reason: Adds Mashaba’s full name and founding role so Herman is not an unexplained reference.

changes.oldText: ActionSA: new party. Still knows the DA’s buttons by heart.
changes.newText: ActionSA: founded by an ex-DA mayor. New party, still knows the DA’s buttons by heart.
changes.meaning: A former DA mayor founded ActionSA, supplying the familiarity behind the metaphor of knowing how to push the DA’s buttons.
changes.reason: Adds the relationship that explains why a new party would know the DA so well.

changes.oldText: ActionSA: the DA breakup that keeps getting renewed for another season.
changes.newText: ActionSA: its founder left the DA. The breakup keeps getting renewed for another season.
changes.meaning: The founder’s departure from the DA is imagined as an ongoing television breakup storyline.
changes.reason: Identifies whose breakup the joke refers to rather than implying ActionSA itself used to be the DA.

changes.oldText: ActionSA: signed a pact with the ex. What could possibly go wrong?
changes.newText: ActionSA: founded by a former DA mayor. Signed a pact with the ex. What could possibly go wrong?
changes.meaning: ActionSA was founded by former DA mayor Herman Mashaba and later signed a national pre-election pact involving the DA, likened to reuniting with an ex.
changes.reason: Explains which party is the ex and why, while keeping the relationship punchline.

changes.oldText: ActionSA: the road to Tshwane’s mayoral office took a sharp ANC turn.
changes.newText: ActionSA: from an anti-ANC pact to ANC help winning Tshwane’s mayoralty. Sharp turn. No indicator.
changes.meaning: ActionSA’s earlier national anti-ANC pact contrasts with ANC support for its Tshwane mayor; the change is imagined as an abrupt road turn.
changes.reason: States both ends of the political turn so the driving metaphor does not require knowledge of the earlier pact.

changes.oldText: ActionSA: kept the mayoral ambition. Changed the supporting cast.
changes.newText: ActionSA: signed an anti-ANC pact, then won Tshwane’s mayoralty with ANC support. Same ambition, new supporting cast.
changes.meaning: The party’s earlier anti-ANC national agreement contrasts with the ANC’s subsequent support for its Tshwane mayor, imagined as a change of cast.
changes.reason: Identifies the actual change in support that the theatrical metaphor previously left unstated.

changes.oldText: ANC + ActionSA in Joburg: commitment issues, but make them a council policy.
changes.newText: ANC + ActionSA in Joburg: support agreed one issue at a time. Commitment issues, now council policy.
changes.meaning: Their limited agreement becomes a relationship-status joke.
changes.reason: Names the issue-by-issue arrangement that makes “commitment issues” a local joke.

changes.oldText: ANC + Al Jama-ah: the junior partner took the master bedroom.
changes.newText: ANC + Al Jama-ah: the small party got Joburg’s mayoral chain. The junior partner took the master bedroom.
changes.meaning: A smaller party secured the leading office.
changes.reason: Identifies the office behind the bedroom metaphor.

changes.oldText: ANC + COPE in Tshwane: barely a caucus. Somehow the head of the table.
changes.newText: ANC + COPE in Tshwane: COPE’s one councillor became mayor. Smallest team, head of the table.
changes.meaning: A one-seat party supplied the mayor.
changes.reason: Supplies the caucus size and mayoral role instead of assuming the player knows them.

changes.oldText:
The office is bigger than the caucus.
ANC and COPE finish the seating plan. Then they notice the mayoral office is bigger than the negotiation room. {actor} reopens the deal by leaving it.
changes.newText:
The office is bigger than the caucus.
ANC and COPE plan a small-party mayor. The office fits all its councillors. The egos need a second room. {actor} reopens the deal by leaving it.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: the fictional negotiation gives a small party a large office and an even larger argument.
changes.reason: Connects the room-size joke to the small-party mayor instead of comparing unrelated rooms.

changes.oldText: ANC + EFF: booked the Tshwane honeymoon. COPE got the suite.
changes.newText: ANC + EFF backed COPE for Tshwane mayor: they booked the honeymoon. COPE got the suite.
changes.meaning: Two parties supported a third party’s mayoral candidate.
changes.reason: Names the support arrangement before the honeymoon punchline.

changes.oldText:
Compromise candidate, uncompromising partners.
ANC and EFF agree neither should take the top job. Both insist on choosing who does. {actor} leaves with the shortlist.
changes.newText:
Compromise candidate, uncompromising partners.
ANC and EFF agree neither should take the mayor’s job. Both insist on choosing who does. {actor} leaves with the shortlist.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: partners fight over choosing a mayor from outside their own parties.
changes.reason: Makes “the top job” explicit.

changes.oldText:
One nomination. Finally.
ANC and EFF settle the nomination before the Speaker finishes calling the meeting to order. All your partners stay. The microphones look underemployed.
changes.newText:
One nomination. Finally.
ANC and EFF settle the mayoral nomination before the Speaker finishes calling the meeting to order. All your partners stay. The microphones look underemployed.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: the nomination is agreed early enough to spare the usual speeches.
changes.reason: Identifies what is being nominated.

changes.oldText: DA + EFF in Ekurhuleni: a mayoral comeback with an awkward thank-you list.
changes.newText: DA + EFF in Ekurhuleni: a DA mayor returned, EFF backing was disputed, and the thank-you list got awkward.
changes.meaning: The disputed account of support makes the comeback’s acknowledgements awkward.
changes.reason: Explains the awkwardness while preserving the dispute about EFF support.

changes.oldText:
Return ticket. Terms apply.
DA and EFF agree on a mayor, then disagree whether support included the return journey. {actor} leaves. The chair is still warm.
changes.newText:
Return ticket. Terms apply.
DA and EFF agree to put a mayor back in office, then disagree whether the support lasts beyond the welcome-back speech. {actor} leaves. The chair is still warm.
changes.meaning: Fictional support for a comeback expires immediately.
changes.reason: Replaces an unexplained “return journey” with a clear mayoral comeback and short-lived support.

changes.oldText: ANC + ABC: Durban’s deputy job came with an ejector seat.
changes.newText: ANC + ABC: Durban’s deputy mayor job came with an ejector seat.
changes.meaning: The deputy mayor was removed from office.
changes.reason: Names the kind of deputy rather than leaving the role implicit.

changes.oldText: DA + IFP in Durban: so united, one stayed off the ballot.
changes.newText: DA + IFP in Durban’s ward 99: so united, the DA stayed off the ballot.
changes.meaning: One party made room for the other in a particular ward election.
changes.reason: Identifies which party stood aside and keeps the ward-level scope clear.

changes.oldText:
After you.
DA and IFP agree who gets this turn. One campaign loudspeaker switches off voluntarily. All your councillors stay.
changes.newText:
After you.
DA and IFP agree which party will stand in this ward. One campaign loudspeaker switches off voluntarily. All your councillors stay.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: cooperation means one campaign voluntarily standing aside.
changes.reason: Explains what “this turn” meant and why a loudspeaker goes quiet.

changes.oldText:
Seven parties, one diary.
DA and ACDP revisit Cape Town’s coalition prequel. The meeting invitation needs seven approvals. {actor} leaves before a date is found.
changes.newText:
Seven parties, one diary.
DA and ACDP revisit their old seven-party Cape Town coalition. The meeting invitation needs seven approvals. {actor} leaves before a date is found.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: a large coalition makes even arranging a meeting difficult.
changes.reason: Puts the seven-party setup in the story itself.

changes.oldText:
The prequel gets a happy ending.
DA and ACDP remember how many calls the old deal took. They answer on the first ring this time. Everyone stays.
changes.newText:
The prequel gets a happy ending.
DA and ACDP remember the seven-party deal and all the calls it took. They answer on the first ring this time. Everyone stays.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: experience with many partners makes cooperation quicker this time.
changes.reason: Explains why the old deal involved so many calls.

changes.oldText: DA + FF+ in Cape Town: seven parties, one bell. FF+ called dibs.
changes.newText: DA + FF+ in Cape Town: FF+ got the Speaker’s chair, keeping seven coalition parties in order. Seven parties, one bell.
changes.meaning: The Speaker must chair a council containing a large coalition.
changes.reason: Names the office and its role so the bell is understandable.

changes.oldText:
The old save file loads.
The DA caucus argues over who gets credit for the city’s coalition origin story. Half of {actor}’s delegation withholds support until the credits are rewritten.
changes.newText:
The old save file loads.
The DA caucus argues over who gets credit for the city’s old seven-party coalition. Half of {actor}’s delegation withholds support until the credits are rewritten.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: the party argues over who deserves credit for its coalition past.
changes.reason: Replaces a vague origin story with the relevant seven-party setup.

changes.oldText: ANC + DA in Mangaung: the ANC caucus took “opposition” a bit too literally.
changes.newText: ANC + DA in Mangaung: some ANC councillors voted for a DA Speaker. Opposition starts at home.
changes.meaning: Some councillors voted against their own party’s choice.
changes.reason: Provides the cross-party vote that makes the opposition joke work.

changes.oldText:
The ballot did not read the memo.
ANC and DA announce that everyone knows the plan. The plan asks for clarification. {actor} leaves before the Speaker gets to nominations.
changes.newText:
The ballot did not read the memo.
ANC and DA announce that everyone knows who to vote for. The councillors ask which of the competing memos to follow. {actor} leaves before nominations close.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: the fictional voting plan falls apart because its instructions conflict.
changes.reason: Replaces an abstract plan asking for clarification with councillors facing contradictory instructions.

changes.oldText:
The votes and the memo agree.
ANC and DA settle the speaking rules before the ballot. Everyone follows the same plan. The whip checks that this is really Mangaung.
changes.newText:
The votes and the memo agree.
ANC and DA agree on a nominee before the ballot. Their councillors follow the plan. The last-minute persuasion speech goes back in the drawer.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: an agreed voting plan removes the need for frantic persuasion.
changes.reason: Makes the agreement about votes and gives the joke a visible payoff without requiring knowledge of Mangaung’s history or a whip’s role.

changes.oldText:
One caucus. One instruction.
The ANC caucus agrees on its position before entering the chamber. The whip briefly runs out of things to worry about. Everyone keeps supporting the deal.
changes.newText:
One caucus. One instruction.
The ANC caucus agrees how its councillors will vote before entering the chamber. The party whip can finally put down the headcount clipboard. Everyone keeps supporting the deal.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: a united caucus gives its vote organiser a break.
changes.reason: Explains what the caucus agrees and gives the whip’s role a practical clue.

changes.oldText: Buffalo City ANC: no opposition required. The recall is coming from inside the house.
changes.newText: Buffalo City ANC: replacing its own mayor. The call is coming from inside the house.
changes.meaning: The governing party replaced its own mayor.
changes.reason: Explains the party replacing its own mayor in plain language, then keeps the familiar call-from-inside-the-house punchline.

changes.oldText: ANC + ATM in Mogale: the junior partner ordered the executive package.
changes.newText: ANC + ATM in Mogale: ATM got the mayor’s office. The junior partner ordered the executive package.
changes.meaning: A smaller coalition partner supplied the mayor.
changes.reason: Names the party and office behind the upgrade joke.

changes.oldText:
The speaking order works.
ANC and EFF agree which jobs belong to which office. For once, the organogram survives the meeting. All your partners stay.
changes.newText:
The speaking order works.
ANC and EFF agree which jobs belong to which office. For once, the job chart survives the meeting. All your partners stay.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: the agreed division of roles survives discussion.
changes.reason: Replaces “organogram” with plain language.

changes.oldText: ANC + PA in Emfuleni: even the biggest caucus needed a longer table.
changes.newText: ANC + PA in Emfuleni: the ANC had the most seats, but still needed a longer negotiating table.
changes.meaning: The largest party still needed other parties’ support.
changes.reason: Explains why the table is growing without suggesting the recorded arrangement reached a majority.

changes.oldText: ANC + PA in JB Marks: one seat short made two seats very popular.
changes.newText: ANC + PA in JB Marks: the ANC was one short of a majority. PA’s two seats had never been so popular.
changes.meaning: Two PA seats could take the ANC past the majority threshold.
changes.reason: Identifies who was short and why two seats mattered.

changes.oldText:
The top-up has terms.
ANC and PA agree on the majority. The final two lines of the agreement take longer than the first twenty. {actor} leaves over the wording.
changes.newText:
The top-up has terms.
ANC and PA agree to combine their seats. The final two lines of the agreement take longer than the first twenty. {actor} leaves over the wording.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: a small addition to the seat total leads to a long negotiation.
changes.reason: Replaces the vague phrase “agree on the majority” with the action being negotiated.

changes.oldText: LCF + EFF in Standerton: the residents’ meeting has developed mayoral ambitions.
changes.newText: Lekwa Community Forum + EFF in Standerton: the residents’ meeting has developed mayoral ambitions.
changes.meaning: A local community party won the mayoralty.
changes.reason: Expands LCF so the residents’ meeting joke works without knowing the acronym.

changes.oldText: ANC + EFF in Sasolburg: local chemistry. Head office said absolutely not.
changes.newText: ANC + EFF in Sasolburg: ANC helped elect an EFF mayor. Local chemistry. EFF head office said absolutely not.
changes.meaning: National leaders rejected local cooperation behind an EFF mayor.
changes.reason: Identifies the local agreement and the party whose head office objected.

changes.oldText:
Everyone cleared the handshake.
ANC and EFF check the local plan with their structures before the meeting. The phones stay silent. Everyone keeps supporting the deal.
changes.newText:
Everyone cleared the handshake.
ANC and EFF check the local plan with their party leaders before the meeting. The phones stay silent. Everyone keeps supporting the deal.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: prior agreement avoids an interrupting call from party leadership.
changes.reason: Replaces the insider term “structures” with the people it means.

changes.oldText: ANC + AIC in Sasolburg: little party, big chain. Must be quite heavy.
changes.newText: ANC + AIC in Sasolburg: little party, big mayoral chain. Must be quite heavy.
changes.meaning: A small party supplied the mayor.
changes.reason: Names the chain as a mayoral chain.

changes.oldText: IFP + Team Sugar: a ballot withdrawal with extra sweetness.
changes.newText: IFP + Team Sugar in Newcastle: IFP stepped off the ward 31 ballot to help its partner. A deal with extra sweetness.
changes.meaning: IFP stood aside in one ward to support Team Sugar.
changes.reason: Supplies which party withdrew, where, and why before the party-name pun.

changes.oldText: IFP in Newcastle’s ward 31: please support us. By voting for someone else.
changes.newText: IFP in Newcastle’s ward 31: please support us. By voting for our partner Team Sugar.
changes.meaning: A party asks supporters to vote for its partner instead.
changes.reason: Names the other party and its relationship to IFP.

changes.oldText:
The campaign team misses the memo.
The IFP delegation debates when to give a partner space. Half has already booked campaign loudspeakers. Half of {actor}’s delegation withholds support while the booking is disputed.
changes.newText:
The campaign team misses the memo.
The IFP delegation debates whether to sit out a ward election for a partner. Half has already booked campaign loudspeakers. Half of {actor}’s delegation withholds support while the booking is disputed.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: a campaign team has prepared to contest a ward it may stand aside in.
changes.reason: Explains what giving a partner space means before the loudspeaker joke.

changes.oldText:
The campaign team gets the memo.
The IFP delegation agrees that cooperation sometimes means taking turns. The loudspeaker booking is sorted, and all your councillors stay.
changes.newText:
The campaign team gets the memo.
The IFP delegation agrees that backing a partner can mean staying off the ballot. The loudspeakers get a day off, and all your councillors stay.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: the delegation accepts an electoral cooperation arrangement.
changes.reason: Makes the campaign decision and the quiet loudspeakers’ payoff explicit.

changes.oldText: IFP + EFF in Richards Bay: perhaps start this reunion with the chairs already labelled.
changes.newText: IFP + EFF in Richards Bay: the last deal broke down. This reunion needs one mayor’s chair and fewer captain’s hats.
changes.meaning: Former partners need to settle leadership before working together again.
changes.reason: Gives the reunion context and identifies the chair without asserting one side’s disputed account as fact.

changes.oldText: DA + IFP in Richards Bay: new deputy, same chair. Mind the previous occupant’s feelings.
changes.newText: DA + IFP in Richards Bay: DA took the deputy’s chair after EFF’s exit. Mind the previous occupant’s feelings.
changes.meaning: The deputy mayor’s office changed parties.
changes.reason: Identifies the previous occupant’s party and the new deputy’s party.

changes.oldText: ANC + ABC in Greytown: Mavundla’s comeback needed a new badge and the old friends.
changes.newText: ANC + ABC in Greytown: former ANC mayor Mavundla returned wearing ABC colours. New badge, old friends.
changes.meaning: A former ANC mayor returned as ABC leader with ANC backing.
changes.reason: Identifies Mavundla’s old and new affiliations before the badge joke.

changes.oldText:
Welcome back. Which badge?
ANC and ABC arrange the Greytown reunion. Someone uses the old party logo on the invitation. {actor} leaves before the welcome speech.
changes.newText:
Welcome back. Which badge?
ANC and ABC arrange a reunion with Mavundla, a former ANC mayor who returned under the ABC badge. Someone uses his old party logo on the invitation. {actor} leaves before the welcome speech.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: a fictional invitation uses a returning politician’s former party branding.
changes.reason: Provides the changed affiliation needed to understand the wrong-logo joke.

changes.oldText: IFP + ABC in Greytown: the reunion invitation should probably mention the ANC.
changes.newText: IFP + ABC in Greytown: ABC left the old deal for the ANC. The reunion invitation should probably mention that.
changes.meaning: Former partners must deal with an earlier switch of allegiance.
changes.reason: Explains why the ANC belongs in a joke about an IFP–ABC reunion.

changes.oldText:
The old chat gets reactivated.
IFP and ABC reopen their old Greytown group chat. The first message is “so, about June”. {actor} leaves before anyone starts typing an apology.
changes.newText:
The old chat gets reactivated.
IFP and ABC reopen their old Greytown group chat. First message: “so, about ABC switching to the ANC…” {actor} leaves before anyone starts typing an apology.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: an awkward reunion immediately raises the previous change of partners.
changes.reason: Replaces the unexplained date “June” with the event itself.

changes.oldText: DA + EFF in Modimolle: heads, principles. Tails, a mayor.
changes.newText: DA + EFF in Modimolle: a tied mayoral vote went to a coin toss. Heads, principles. Tails, a mayor.
changes.meaning: A coin toss really settled a tied mayoral election.
changes.reason: States the unusual event before the heads-or-tails punchline.

changes.oldText:
Heads, we need another meeting.
DA and EFF remember the famous coin toss. This time they cannot agree who gets to call it. {actor} leaves. Your seats are still counted normally.
changes.newText:
Heads, we need another meeting.
DA and EFF remember the mayoral election settled by a coin toss. This time they cannot agree who gets to call it. {actor} leaves. Your seats are still counted normally.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: the fictional partners cannot even agree how to organise their old tiebreaker.
changes.reason: Explains what the “famous coin toss” decided.

changes.oldText:
Leave the coin in your pocket.
DA and EFF agree on the work plan before anyone asks for loose change. Everyone keeps supporting the deal. This roll needs no historical tiebreaker.
changes.newText:
Leave the coin in your pocket.
DA and EFF remember that a coin once settled the mayor’s job. This time, they agree on the plan before anyone asks for loose change. Everyone keeps supporting the deal.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: agreement avoids repeating the historical need for a random tiebreaker.
changes.reason: Places the coin’s historical role directly in the story.

changes.oldText: DA + FF+ in Modimolle: when the kingmaker is loose change.
changes.newText: DA + FF+ in Modimolle: a coin toss settled the tied mayoral vote. The kingmaker was loose change.
changes.meaning: A coin decided who became mayor after a tie.
changes.reason: Explains why loose change could be a kingmaker.

changes.oldText:
The coin needs a subcommittee.
DA and FF+ agree they should be prepared. The proposed tiebreaker coin needs three sign-offs. {actor} leaves before the procurement form is complete.
changes.newText:
The coin needs a subcommittee.
DA and FF+ remember the tied mayoral election settled by a coin toss. Their emergency coin now needs three sign-offs. {actor} leaves before the procurement form is complete.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: a fictional emergency tiebreaker gets buried in bureaucracy.
changes.reason: Explains why the partners are trying to procure a coin.

changes.oldText:
Agreement beats loose change.
DA and FF+ settle the plan in writing. The emergency coin stays in a drawer. Everyone keeps supporting the deal.
changes.newText:
Agreement beats loose change.
DA and FF+ remember needing a coin toss to settle a tied mayoral vote. This time they settle the plan in writing. The emergency coin stays in a drawer. Everyone keeps supporting the deal.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: an agreed plan makes the old tiebreaker unnecessary.
changes.reason: Explains why an emergency coin exists.

changes.oldText: DA + NCM in Springbok: musical chairs with a playlist everyone signed.
changes.newText: DA + NCM in Springbok: the mayor and Speaker agreed to swap jobs. Musical chairs, with a signed playlist.
changes.meaning: The parties arranged a rotation of two offices.
changes.reason: Identifies which chairs were being swapped.

changes.oldText:
The office swap hits a snag.
DA and NCM agree it is time to swap offices. Both want to keep the chair with good back support. {actor} leaves before moving day.
changes.newText:
The office swap hits a snag.
DA and NCM agree it is time to swap the mayor and Speaker’s offices. Both want to keep the chair with good back support. {actor} leaves before moving day.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: an agreed role swap is fictionally derailed by office furniture.
changes.reason: Names the roles behind the office swap.

changes.oldText:
Musical chairs, as scheduled.
DA and NCM swap roles exactly as agreed. Even the pot plants make it to the right offices. Everyone stays in the deal.
changes.newText:
Musical chairs, as scheduled.
DA and NCM swap the mayor and Speaker roles exactly as agreed. Even the pot plants make it to the right offices. Everyone stays in the deal.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: the agreed role rotation runs smoothly.
changes.reason: Names the roles rather than relying on the backstory.

changes.oldText: DA + UDM in the Bay: the deputy mayor’s chair has abandonment issues.
changes.newText: DA + UDM in the Bay: UDM’s deputy mayor was voted out. His chair has abandonment issues.
changes.meaning: Removal of the deputy mayor becomes a furniture joke.
changes.reason: Explains why the chair has been abandoned.

changes.oldText:
The deputy chair squeaks.
DA and UDM discuss who sits where. The deputy mayor’s chair makes a noise suspiciously like “remember 2017?” {actor} leaves the deal.
changes.newText:
The deputy chair squeaks.
DA and UDM discuss who sits where. The deputy mayor’s chair remembers the last no-confidence vote and starts squeaking. {actor} leaves the deal.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: the furniture dreads another removal vote.
changes.reason: Replaces “remember 2017?” with the event being remembered.

changes.oldText: DA + ACDP in George: prayers answered. The answer was Corporate Services.
changes.newText: DA + ACDP in George: ACDP got the Corporate Services portfolio. Even answered prayers come with paperwork.
changes.meaning: Receiving a council portfolio also means taking on its work.
changes.reason: Explains what Corporate Services refers to before the prayer-and-paperwork punchline.

changes.oldText:
The portfolio comes with paperwork.
DA and ACDP settle the title, then see the pile of forms that comes with it. {actor} leaves to renegotiate the meaning of “shared responsibility”.
changes.newText:
The portfolio comes with paperwork.
DA and ACDP settle who gets the Corporate Services portfolio, then see the pile of forms that comes with it. {actor} leaves to renegotiate the meaning of “shared responsibility”.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: an agreed political role brings an unwelcome pile of fictional paperwork.
changes.reason: Identifies the title being allocated.

changes.oldText: ANC + FF+ in Oudtshoorn: awkward enough to make an ostrich look away.
changes.newText: ANC + FF+ in Oudtshoorn: campaign opponents now sharing power. Awkward enough to make an ostrich look away.
changes.meaning: Former electoral opponents must now cooperate in government.
changes.reason: Explains the source of the awkwardness without requiring familiarity with party ideologies.

changes.oldText:
The campaign leaflet resurfaces.
ANC and FF+ agree to work together. Someone leaves last election’s campaign leaflet on the meeting table. {actor} leaves before page two.
changes.newText:
The campaign leaflet resurfaces.
ANC and FF+ agree to work together. Someone leaves a campaign leaflet criticising the other party on the meeting table. {actor} leaves before page two.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: a fictional campaign attack becomes awkward after the parties agree to cooperate.
changes.reason: Explains why the leaflet is embarrassing.

changes.oldText: DA + FF+ in Oudtshoorn: still untangling the feathers from the last breakup.
changes.newText: DA + FF+ in Oudtshoorn: FF+ helped remove the DA mayor. Still untangling feathers from that breakup.
changes.meaning: A previous coalition partner supported the mayor’s removal.
changes.reason: Names the event behind the breakup while keeping the local feather joke.

changes.oldText: ANC + GOOD in Theewaterskloof: GOOD company. Until it found other company.
changes.newText: ANC + GOOD in Theewaterskloof: GOOD switched from the ANC’s side to the DA’s. GOOD company, until it found other company.
changes.meaning: GOOD changed which side it supported.
changes.reason: Explains the party switch behind the company pun.

changes.oldText: DA + GOOD in Theewaterskloof: the ANC’s ex says you’re different.
changes.newText: DA + GOOD in Theewaterskloof: GOOD came over from the ANC’s side. The ANC’s ex says you’re different.
changes.meaning: A former ANC partner starts working with the DA.
changes.reason: Identifies whose former partner is arriving.

changes.oldText: DA + PDC in Plett: your coalition partner checked into the other mayoral suite.
changes.newText: DA + PDC in Plett: PDC left the deal and took the mayor’s office with new partners. Checked into the other suite.
changes.meaning: The departing coalition partner supplied the next mayor.
changes.reason: Explains the political move behind the hotel metaphor.

changes.oldText: ANC + PA in Plett: the coalition unpacked before checking the cancellation policy.
changes.newText: ANC + PA in Plett: a short-lived coalition that unpacked before checking the cancellation policy.
changes.meaning: The governing arrangement changed again within the year.
changes.reason: Signals the arrangement’s short life before the accommodation joke.

changes.oldText: ANC + PA in Beaufort West: the mayoral chain gets more mileage than the N1.
changes.newText: ANC + PA in Beaufort West: five mayors in under three years. The mayoral chain gets more mileage than the N1.
changes.meaning: Repeated mayoral changes mean the chain keeps moving.
changes.reason: Supplies the turnover behind the mileage joke.

changes.oldText: DA + Cederberg First: the reunion needed a by-election, not just a group chat.
changes.newText: DA + Cederberg First: getting their mayor back took a by-election. Some reunions need more than a group chat.
changes.meaning: A by-election result enabled former partners to return to office.
changes.reason: Explains what the reunion achieved and why the election mattered.

changes.oldText:
The comeback needs a map.
DA and Cederberg First attempt the reunion route. They disagree at the first turn marked “last time”. {actor} takes the off-ramp.
changes.newText:
The comeback needs a map.
DA and Cederberg First plan a coalition comeback. The route map has a turn marked “where we fell out last time”. {actor} takes the off-ramp.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: the old coalition’s problems reappear on a fictional reunion route.
changes.reason: Explains the comeback and replaces a vague “last time” sign with its meaning.

changes.oldText: DA + FF+ in Swellendam: one abstention. The whole seating plan needed therapy.
changes.newText: DA + FF+ in Swellendam: one councillor abstained and the mayoral vote tied. The seating plan needed therapy.
changes.meaning: An abstention left the election tied.
changes.reason: Names the consequence of the abstention without confusing it with the later resignation.

changes.oldText: DA + FF+ in Saldanha: one seat. Suddenly everyone remembers your birthday.
changes.newText: DA + FF+ in Saldanha: FF+’s one seat completed a majority. Suddenly everyone remembers your birthday.
changes.meaning: A single-seat partner supplied decisive support.
changes.reason: Explains why one seat suddenly attracts so much attention.

changes.oldText: Witzenberg’s DA: kept the receipt for the mayoral chair.
changes.newText: Witzenberg’s DA: back in the mayor’s office. Good thing it kept the receipt for the chair.
changes.meaning: The DA returned to the mayoralty.
changes.reason: Names the comeback behind the returned-furniture joke.

changes.oldText: DA + FF+ in Langeberg: irreconcilable differences, itemised.
changes.newText: DA + FF+ in Langeberg: a budget dispute and a coalition breakup. Irreconcilable differences, itemised.
changes.meaning: A budget argument featured in the account of a coalition breakup.
changes.reason: Explains why the differences are itemised without assigning blame.

changes.oldText: ANC + ICOSA: the local honeymoon lasted until the provincial office phoned.
changes.newText: ANC + ICOSA: ANC’s provincial leaders ordered an end to the local deal. Honeymoon cancelled by head office.
changes.meaning: Provincial party instructions ended a local arrangement.
changes.reason: Identifies whose leaders called and what they required.

changes.oldText:
A memo arrives from upstairs.
ANC and ICOSA finish the local agreement just as another instruction arrives. The documents disagree. {actor} leaves to find out which one applies.
changes.newText:
A memo arrives from upstairs.
ANC and ICOSA finish the local agreement just as ANC’s provincial office sends the opposite instruction. The documents disagree. {actor} leaves to find out which one applies.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: local and provincial instructions conflict in the fictional deal.
changes.reason: Identifies the source of the instruction arriving “from upstairs”.

changes.oldText:
Local knowledge. Different directions.
DA and KIM both know the way around Knysna. They disagree on the route to an agreement. {actor} leaves before anyone reaches the Heads.
changes.newText:
Local knowledge. Different directions.
DA and KIM both know the way around Knysna. They disagree on the route to an agreement. {actor} takes a turn marked “exit”.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: the negotiation’s route map ends in a walkout.
changes.reason: Replaces a punchline dependent on knowing the Knysna Heads with an immediately readable route joke.

changes.oldText:
The red lines enter the chat.
DA and EFF sit down to negotiate. Someone brings a folder of old campaign speeches. {actor} leaves before the folder is opened.
changes.newText:
The campaign insults enter the chat.
DA and EFF sit down to negotiate. Someone brings a folder of the insults they traded during the campaign. {actor} leaves before the folder is opened.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: the negotiations are derailed before the parties even open a folder of the insults they traded while campaigning.
changes.reason: Names the campaign insults behind the red-line and old-speeches references; the approved tease is unchanged.

changes.oldText:
The water pipes win this round.
DA and EFF put the speeches aside and agree on the water-pipe repairs. The work plan has fewer exclamation marks. Everyone stays.
changes.newText:
The water pipes win this round.
DA and EFF put the old campaign insults aside and agree on the water-pipe repairs. The work plan has fewer exclamation marks. Everyone stays.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: putting campaign insults aside produces a calmer repair plan with fewer exclamation marks.
changes.reason: Names which speeches are being set aside so the punctuation joke has a clear setup.

changes.oldText: DA + MK: Helen’s nightmare now has a seating plan.
changes.newText: DA + MK: the DA’s Helen Zille doubted this match. You’ve arranged the date.
changes.meaning: Helen Zille’s doubt about DA–MK cooperation becomes an awkward date arranged by the player.
changes.reason: Identifies Helen Zille with the DA and states her earlier doubt before the matchmaking joke.

changes.oldText:
The seating plan crosses a red line.
DA and MK approve the seat totals, then discover their delegations are expected to share a table. {actor} leaves to consult the campaign archive.
changes.newText:
Enough seats. Wrong neighbour.
DA and MK approve your deal’s seat totals. Then they see they’ll be sitting next to each other. {actor} leaves before the place cards are printed.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: the numbers work for the fictional deal, but sharing the table with a political opponent proves harder.
changes.reason: Replaces an unexplained campaign-archive reference with the visible problem of sitting together.

changes.oldText: DA + ActionSA: Joburg’s exes are trying again. Hide the old screenshots.
changes.newText: DA + ActionSA: Joburg’s coalition exes are trying again. Hide the old screenshots.
changes.meaning: Former coalition partners are treated as exes trying again, with old screenshots ready to reopen arguments.
changes.reason: Adds coalition to explain what kind of exes these parties are while keeping the relationship joke.

changes.oldText:
The exes agree on something.
DA and ActionSA put the old Joburg arguments in a folder marked “after the election”. Everyone stays. Nobody deletes the screenshots.
changes.newText:
The coalition exes agree on something.
DA and ActionSA put the old Joburg arguments in a folder marked “after the election”. Everyone stays. Nobody deletes the screenshots.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: the coalition exes postpone their old arguments but keep the screenshots.
changes.reason: Adds coalition so the title explains the exes metaphor without needing the backstory.

changes.oldText: DA + ActionSA in Tshwane: same exes, same keys, fresh trust issues.
changes.newText: DA + ActionSA in Tshwane: coalition exes. Same office keys, fresh trust issues.
changes.meaning: Former coalition partners return to familiar offices with lingering trust issues.
changes.reason: Names the coalition relationship and specifies office keys while retaining the exes joke.

changes.oldText: ANC + ActionSA: Tshwane’s anti-ANC speeches have been placed on unpaid leave.
changes.newText: ANC + ActionSA: ANC votes helped elect ActionSA’s Tshwane mayor. The anti-ANC speeches are on unpaid leave.
changes.meaning: ANC votes helping elect an ActionSA mayor put earlier anti-ANC speeches on imaginary unpaid leave.
changes.reason: Adds the vote and mayoral outcome that make the unpaid-leave joke understandable.

changes.oldText:
Local politics, different playlist.
ANC and ActionSA agree to share the credit for fixing the roads. Two logos fit on the announcement. Everyone stays.
changes.newText:
Both logos fit.
ANC and ActionSA agree to share the credit for fixing the roads. Two logos fit on the announcement. Everyone stays.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: sharing credit for road repairs turns out to be as simple as fitting both logos on an announcement.
changes.reason: Connects the title to the logos in the story instead of an unexplained playlist metaphor.

changes.oldText:
GNU, but make it municipal.
ANC and DA draft a joint statement. The tracked changes develop tracked changes. {actor} leaves before they agree on the first sentence.
changes.newText:
Same rivals. Smaller meeting room.
ANC and DA draft a joint statement. The tracked changes develop tracked changes. {actor} leaves before they agree on the first sentence.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: national rivals take their arguments into a local meeting and cannot finish one joint statement.
changes.reason: Replaces the unexplained GNU acronym with the smaller local meeting that the scenario depicts.

changes.oldText:
A GNU day at the office.
ANC and DA agree on the council agenda. Both claim to have written it. Everyone stays, so Madam Speaker lets that one slide.
changes.newText:
Two authors. One agenda.
ANC and DA agree on the council agenda. Both claim to have written it. Everyone stays, so Madam Speaker lets that one slide.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: both parties claim authorship of the agreed agenda, but the council can get to work.
changes.reason: Makes the title match the authorship joke without relying on the GNU/new-day pun.

changes.oldText: ANC + MK: family reunion. Bring your own faction.
changes.newText: ANC + MK: Jacob Zuma’s old party meets his new one. Bring your own grudge.
changes.meaning: Jacob Zuma’s old and new parties turn a political reunion into a family gathering with old grudges.
changes.reason: Names the person linking the parties so the family metaphor has an explicit setup.

changes.oldText: DA + FF+: the anti-ANC carpool now stops at Cabinet.
changes.newText: DA + FF+: the anti-ANC carpool now stops at Cabinet. The ANC is already inside.
changes.meaning: The parties’ anti-ANC carpool reaches a Cabinet that also contains the ANC.
changes.reason: Adds the contradiction that makes the carpool joke work.

changes.oldText: DA + PA: one GNU, two parties refusing to let the other finish a sentence.
changes.newText: DA + PA: one unity government, two parties refusing to let the other finish a sentence.
changes.meaning: Parties in one unity government still compete to finish every sentence first.
changes.reason: Expands the GNU acronym into ordinary language while preserving the interruption joke.

changes.oldText:
The microphone is not a portfolio.
DA and PA hold a joint briefing. Both want the last word. {actor} withdraws its support and leaves the other party with the microphone.
changes.newText:
The microphone is not a job title.
DA and PA hold a joint briefing. Both want the last word. {actor} withdraws its support and leaves the other party with the microphone.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: the parties treat control of a shared briefing microphone like a council job to fight over.
changes.reason: Replaces the specialised portfolio term with job title.

changes.oldText: ANC + EFF in the Bay: they brought the votes. Someone else got the big chair.
changes.newText: ANC + EFF in the Bay: they brought the votes. The Northern Alliance got the mayor’s chair.
changes.meaning: ANC and EFF supplied support for a mayor from the Northern Alliance rather than either of their own parties.
changes.reason: Names the third party and the mayor’s office behind the big-chair reference.

changes.oldText: ANC + PA in Knysna: a fresh start, with the appointments item underlined.
changes.newText: ANC + PA in Knysna: PA says hiring decisions sank the last deal. This time, that agenda item is double-underlined.
changes.meaning: The PA’s stated reason for the earlier breakup makes hiring an anxiously emphasised item on the fictional reunion agenda.
changes.reason: State the previous dispute and retain attribution to the PA, so the double-underlining joke works without reading the backstory.

changes.oldText:
The lagoon is the calm part.
ANC and PA promise a quiet Knysna meeting. Then the appointments item arrives. {actor} leaves before anyone reaches “any other business”.
changes.newText:
The lagoon is the calm part.
ANC and PA promise a quiet Knysna meeting. Then the staff appointments item arrives. {actor} leaves before anyone reaches “any other business”.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: the calm meeting breaks down when staff appointments reach the agenda.
changes.reason: Specifies staff appointments so the disputed topic is clear.

changes.oldText:
An agreement with a view.
ANC and PA agree on the appointments process before debating office views. The meeting ends with all partners still in the room.
changes.newText:
An agreement with a view.
ANC and PA agree on the staff appointments process before debating office views. The meeting ends with all partners still in the room.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: settling the staff appointments process leaves the parties free to argue about office views.
changes.reason: Specifies staff appointments so the agreement and office-view joke have a clear sequence.

changes.oldText: ANC + EFF in Durban: revolutionary until the mayor needs a favour.
changes.newText: ANC + EFF in Durban: the EFF’s revolution can wait. The ANC mayor needs their votes.
changes.meaning: The EFF’s revolutionary image is contrasted with its votes helping an ANC mayor survive.
changes.reason: Names whose revolution, whose mayor and which favour the joke refers to.

changes.oldText:
Confidence has left the building.
ANC and EFF agree that confidence is essential. They disagree on who should have it. {actor} leaves the Durban deal.
changes.newText:
Confidence has left the building.
ANC and EFF agree the mayor must have everyone’s confidence. Then they name two different people. {actor} leaves the Durban deal.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: both parties demand confidence in the mayor, then choose different people for the job.
changes.reason: Turns an abstract disagreement about confidence into a concrete fictional disagreement over the mayor.

changes.oldText: DA + ActionSA: signed the pact. Kept the grudge.
changes.newText: DA + ActionSA: signed the anti-ANC pact. Kept the grudge.
changes.meaning: Signing a common anti-ANC pact does not magically erase the partners’ old arguments.
changes.reason: Names the pact’s purpose so the joke does not require Charter knowledge.

changes.oldText: DA + IFP: the anti-ANC pact took a scenic route through the GNU.
changes.newText: DA + IFP: the anti-ANC pact took a scenic route into a government with the ANC.
changes.meaning: A pact aimed at replacing the ANC takes a scenic detour into government with the ANC.
changes.reason: Explains the later ANC-inclusive government instead of relying on the GNU acronym.

changes.oldText:
The pact needs an annexure.
DA and IFP agree on the big picture. The local seating plan requires another annexure. {actor} leaves while it is still being drafted.
changes.newText:
The small print gets bigger.
DA and IFP agree on the big picture. Who gets which council job needs another page. {actor} leaves while it is still being drafted.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: agreement on broad aims unravels over which party gets which council job, making the paperwork grow.
changes.reason: Replaces annexure and an abstract seating plan with the actual fictional allocation of council jobs.

changes.oldText:
The annexure is only one page.
DA and IFP approve a local agreement shorter than the meeting agenda. Everyone signs. Nobody requests a subcommittee.
changes.newText:
The fine print fits on one page.
DA and IFP approve a local agreement shorter than the meeting agenda. Everyone signs. Nobody requests a subcommittee.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: the partners finally produce an agreement shorter than the meeting agenda and resist creating another committee.
changes.reason: Replaces annexure with the familiar fine-print metaphor.

changes.oldText: ANC + PA: the GNU is a team sport. Both have appointed themselves captain.
changes.newText: ANC + PA: unity government is a team sport. Both have appointed themselves captain.
changes.meaning: The parties treat unity government as a team sport while both claiming the captaincy.
changes.reason: Expands the GNU acronym without changing the competing-captains joke.

changes.oldText:
The handshake needs a schedule.
ANC and PA agree to share the stage. Then they compare speaking times. {actor} leaves before the ribbon has been found.
changes.newText:
The handshake needs a schedule.
ANC and PA agree to share the stage at their coalition launch. Then they compare speaking times. {actor} leaves before the microphones are switched on.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: sharing a coalition-launch stage breaks down over speaking time before the microphones are switched on.
changes.reason: Establishes the event and uses its microphones for the ending instead of introducing an unexplained ribbon.

changes.oldText:
The national handshake needs a local sequel.
ANC and IFP bring their GNU group photo to the meeting. It does not answer who gets the local office. {actor} leaves to renegotiate.
changes.newText:
The national handshake needs a local sequel.
ANC and IFP bring a photo of their national unity government. It does not say who gets the local mayor’s office. {actor} leaves to renegotiate.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: a national unity-government photo cannot settle which local partner gets the mayor’s office.
changes.reason: Expands GNU and names the local mayoral job instead of an unspecified office; this remains a fictional local scenario.

changes.oldText: ANC + FF+: even the old campaign posters have requested a transfer.
changes.newText: ANC + FF+: former opponents, Cabinet colleagues. The old campaign posters have requested a transfer.
changes.meaning: Old campaign posters would rather transfer than watch former opponents become Cabinet colleagues.
changes.reason: States the former-opponents/new-colleagues contrast before the personified posters react.

changes.oldText: IFP + PA: Hlabisa tries to cooperate. Gayton appeals to the referee.
changes.newText: IFP + PA: IFP’s Hlabisa got Cooperative Governance. PA’s Gayton got Sport. They still need a referee.
changes.meaning: The parties received Cooperative Governance and Sport portfolios, yet their imaginary coalition talks still need a referee.
changes.reason: Identifies each politician’s party and portfolio so the cooperation and sporting wordplay is explicit.

changes.oldText: IFP + FF+: left to stop the ANC. Came home with GNU lanyards.
changes.newText: IFP + FF+: signed an anti-ANC pact. Then joined a Cabinet with the ANC. Please update the lanyards.
changes.meaning: The parties’ move from an anti-ANC pact into an ANC-inclusive Cabinet makes their lanyards need updating.
changes.reason: Spells out the change in political company behind the GNU-lanyard joke.
