changes.oldText: PA + FF+: Sport meets Correctional Services. Extra time has two meanings.
changes.newText: PA + FF+: Sport meets the prisons portfolio. Extra time has two meanings.
changes.meaning: Extra time means more play in sport but more time served in prison.
changes.reason: Explains Correctional Services as the prisons portfolio so both meanings are accessible.

changes.oldText: IFP + ActionSA: the old pact is back. Please ignore where everyone went afterwards.
changes.newText: IFP + ActionSA: signed an anti-ANC pact. Later worked with the ANC. Please face the camera.
changes.meaning: Parties that signed an anti-ANC pact later worked with the ANC, making the reunion photo awkward.
changes.reason: States the later political choice instead of asking the player to know where everyone went.

changes.oldText:
The reunion finishes its homework.
IFP and ActionSA agree that the local roads need a new plan, even if the party badges are familiar. Everyone signs and stays.
changes.newText:
The reunion finishes its homework.
IFP and ActionSA agree on the road repairs and put deadlines in writing. Everyone stays. The calendar has joined the coalition.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: the reunion produces actual road-repair deadlines, making the calendar an imaginary new coalition partner.
changes.reason: Gives the homework title a concrete payoff instead of an unexplained reference to familiar badges.

changes.oldText: FF+ + ActionSA: the anti-ANC pact has some awkward post-election photos.
changes.newText: FF+ + ActionSA: anti-ANC pact, then ANC partners. The old group photo needs a new caption.
changes.meaning: An old anti-ANC group photo needs a new caption after both parties later work with the ANC.
changes.reason: Makes the change in partners explicit before the photo-caption punchline.

changes.oldText:

FF+ and ActionSA agree that the local roads need a new plan, even if the party badges are familiar. Everyone signs and stays.

changes.oldText: EFF + MK: please check which side Floyd was on when that photo was taken.
changes.newText: EFF + MK: Floyd Shivambu moved from EFF to MK. Please date the group photos.
changes.meaning: Floyd Shivambu’s move from EFF to MK makes the date on an old group photo essential.
changes.reason: Names Floyd fully and states the party transfer before the photo joke.

changes.oldText:
The old name tags come out.
EFF and MK agree to look forward. Someone brings the 2024 group photo. {actor} leaves before the introductions are finished.
changes.newText:
The group photo needs a date.
EFF and MK agree to look forward. Someone brings a group photo from before Floyd Shivambu left EFF for MK. {actor} leaves before the introductions are finished.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: an old photo from before Shivambu changed parties interrupts a meeting that was supposed to look forward.
changes.reason: Explains why the old photo is awkward and aligns the title with that prop.

changes.oldText:
The reunion skips the awkward bit.
EFF and MK put the old party badges away and agree on the water repairs. Everyone stays. No transfer-window questions at the briefing.
changes.newText:
The reunion skips the awkward bit.
EFF and MK put the old party badges away and agree on the water repairs. Everyone stays. Questions about who joined whom can wait.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: the parties get on with repairs while putting awkward questions about changing parties aside.
changes.reason: Replaces the transfer-window reference with plain language about who joined whom.

changes.oldText: EFF + IFP: reunited. Please don’t ask who gets uMhlathuze.
changes.newText: EFF + IFP: last time, there was a row over uMhlathuze’s mayor’s job. This time, hide the chair.
changes.meaning: A previous argument over uMhlathuze’s mayoral job makes hiding the chair seem like preparation for this reunion.
changes.reason: States the earlier mayoral-job dispute before the chair joke without assigning blame or claiming it was the sole reason for the breakup.

changes.oldText:
A different chair, a different ending.
EFF and IFP settle the speaking order and the repairs programme. Nobody reopens the 2023 argument. Everyone stays.
changes.newText:
A different chair, a different ending.
EFF and IFP agree who chairs the meeting and which roads get repaired. Nobody reopens the old fight over who gets the mayor’s job. Everyone stays.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: the partners settle the chairing and repairs instead of reopening their old mayoral-job dispute.
changes.reason: States what the 2023 argument concerned instead of requiring the player to remember it.

changes.oldText:
The invitation meets the old conditions.
EFF and FF+ sit down. Someone reads the 2024 GNU conditions aloud. {actor} leaves before the welcome drinks.
changes.newText:
The invitation meets the old conditions.
EFF and FF+ sit down. Someone remembers that in 2024, the EFF ruled out sharing the national government with FF+. {actor} leaves before the welcome drinks.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: a fictional meeting becomes awkward when someone remembers the EFF’s dated opposition to sharing national government with FF+.
changes.reason: Explains the specific 2024 condition while preserving its date and national scope.

changes.oldText: ANC + EFF: dinner for two. Julius has opinions about the other guests.
changes.newText: ANC + EFF: dinner for two. EFF leader Julius Malema has opinions about the DA and FF+ plus-ones.
changes.meaning: A dinner invitation becomes awkward because EFF leader Julius Malema objected to DA and FF+ joining the arrangement.
changes.reason: Identifies Julius, his party role and the unwanted plus-ones without inventing attributed dialogue.

changes.oldText: ActionSA + MK: Herman’s open to talks. His eyebrows have reservations.
changes.newText: ActionSA + MK: ActionSA leader Herman Mashaba is open to talks. His eyebrows have reservations.
changes.meaning: Mashaba is open to talking while his personified eyebrows remain unconvinced.
changes.reason: Identifies Herman Mashaba and his ActionSA role before the facial-expression joke.

changes.oldText: IFP + MK: one won the biggest bloc, the other got the keys. Lovely reunion.
changes.newText: IFP + MK: MK won the most KZN seats. IFP got the premier’s job. Lovely reunion.
changes.meaning: MK won the most provincial seats, but IFP won the premier’s job, making their reunion awkward.
changes.reason: Names which party got which electoral outcome and office instead of using ambiguous keys and blocs.

changes.oldText: EFF + ActionSA in Tshwane: the red line turned out to be a red carpet.
changes.newText: EFF + ActionSA in Tshwane: from an anti-EFF pact to EFF votes for ActionSA’s mayor. Roll out the red carpet.
changes.meaning: An earlier aim to keep EFF out becomes a welcome for EFF votes helping elect ActionSA’s mayor.
changes.reason: Supplies the reversal that makes the red-carpet joke work.

changes.oldText: PA + ActionSA in Joburg: the reported reunion offer came with two portfolios.
changes.newText: PA + ActionSA in Joburg: ActionSA says it offered PA two council leadership jobs. Some welcome-back cards come with job titles.
changes.meaning: ActionSA’s reported offer to bring PA back included two leadership jobs, making the welcome-back card unusually practical.
changes.reason: Keeps the proposal attributed to ActionSA and explains portfolios as council leadership jobs; it does not claim those posts were received.

changes.oldText:
The welcome-back package needs work.
PA and ActionSA discuss the office allocation. The welcome-back card has more conditions than signatures. {actor} leaves to make a counteroffer.
changes.newText:
The welcome-back package needs work.
PA and ActionSA discuss who gets which council job. The welcome-back card has more conditions than signatures. {actor} leaves to make a counteroffer.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: a welcome-back offer becomes a negotiation over council jobs with more conditions than signatures.
changes.reason: Names the council jobs behind office allocation.

changes.oldText:
The caucus has two endings.
ANC agrees on the history but not the next chapter. Half of {actor}’s delegation withholds support until someone rewrites the plan.
changes.newText:
One party. Two plans.
ANC’s councillors agree on the party name, then bring two different plans for the council. Half of {actor}’s delegation withholds support until they pick one.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: councillors agree on their party name but cannot agree on one council plan, so half the delegation withholds support.
changes.reason: Makes the internal single-party disagreement concrete while preserving the half-delegation mechanic and actor placeholder.

changes.oldText:
A new chapter everyone signs.
ANC puts the old speeches aside and agrees on the next repairs. All your councillors stay.
changes.newText:
One party. One signed plan.
ANC’s councillors agree which repairs come first and sign the same plan. All your councillors stay. Even the pens get a round of applause.
changes.meaning: Invented scene: agreement on one repair plan earns even the signing pens an imaginary round of applause.
changes.reason: Replaces vague book-history references with a clear repair-plan agreement while keeping all councillors in the deal.
